---

**The Infamous Anecdote: Documented Reality vs. Contested Attribution**

The quote attributed to President Lyndon B. Johnson--"I'll have those [n-words] voting Democratic for the next two hundred years"--has circulated widely in political discourse for decades. According to investigative journalist Ronald Kessler's 1995 book '[Inside the White House](https://substack.com/redirect/aa181936-eb64-4d43-a65d-0bb25ead77c3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)', this remark originated from Air Force One steward Robert MacMillan, who claimed Johnson uttered these words during a conversation with two governors aboard the presidential aircraft following the signing of the Civil Rights Act of 1964.

The anecdote's historical veracity remains deeply contested. Fact-checkers at Snopes have categorized the quote as unverified, noting that while MacMillan provided numerous salacious details about Johnson's personal behavior--including his habit of walking around nude in front of staff--the sole witness to the alleged remark lacks corroboration. Luci Baines Johnson, the president's daughter, explicitly denied another claim by MacMillan involving offensive language, raising questions about the steward's credibility. Nevertheless, Snopes acknowledged that such language "wouldn't have been entirely out of character for LBJ," given his well-documented history of using racial slurs and coarse political calculations.

What is historically certain is Johnson's political pessimism regarding civil rights legislation. His famous remark to aide Bill Moyers on the night he signed the Civil Rights Act--that "we just delivered the South to the Republican party for a long time to come"--is extensively documented and reveals the president's awareness that supporting civil rights would trigger a seismic political realignment that would fracture the Democratic Party's century-long dominance in the South.

**The Box 13 Scandal: Foundation of a Political Career**

To understand Johnson's relationship with electoral systems, one must examine the [Box 13 scandal](https://substack.com/redirect/0ad8b81d-1a1d-4ab9-95a0-3d414217d50a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of 1948--a genuine electoral fraud that launched his national political career. In the 1948 Democratic Senate primary runoff, Johnson trailed former Texas Governor Coke Stevenson by 854 votes with 99 percent of precincts counted. Then, in a manner reminiscent of a dramatic screenplay or [Seattle elections](https://substack.com/redirect/75f3af3d-e128-4454-ac22-10824bd53b18?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this decade, Precinct 13 in Jim Wells County reported exactly 200 additional votes for Johnson, awarding him an 87-vote victory.

The circumstances were [extraordinarily suspicious](https://substack.com/redirect/92a8dae6-0edc-469f-822b-be94a6c0268b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Those 200 votes appeared in alphabetical order, all recorded by the same handwriting. LBJ reportedly told his aide John Connally, "I want to know right now, did we steal this election or not?" The answer was yes: an investigation subsequently confirmed that Johnson had conspired with George Parr, the Democratic political boss of South Texas known as "the Duke of Duval County," to manufacture votes in the final hours of the count. Parr famously told election officials, "Keep those polls open until we get the results we need."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/daefe56d-f5a9-4c3f-be05-490dcde6e35a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
This proven history of electoral manipulation established Johnson's nickname "Landslide Lyndon"--ironically bestowed--and demonstrated his intimate understanding of how political machines could control vote counts in precincts with weak oversight.

Following his narrow and controversial 1948 election victory, Lyndon Johnson transformed himself from "Landslide Lyndon" into perhaps the most effective Senate Majority Leader in American history, earning him the enduring epithet "[Master of the Senate](https://substack.com/redirect/2d5190cf-51f0-4434-98fc-24f45f838f49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)." When Democrats regained control of the Senate in 1955, Johnson seized the Majority Leader's position--a role his predecessor had described as herding cats--and reimagined it into an engine of legislative power through an unprecedented combination of procedural cunning, psychological manipulation, and tireless coalition-building. He mastered the Senate's labyrinthine rules to an extent no modern leader has matched, strategically deploying the filibuster and cloture while manipulating the committee system through his control of the Democratic Steering Committee. Johnson's legendary "treatment"--a combination of physical intimidation, flattery, and exhaustive bargaining delivered through inches-away face-to-face encounters--allowed him to break deadlock and forge compromise on civil rights legislation, public housing, and atomic energy, even as his heartbreaking 1957 and 1960 civil rights bills were watered down to appease Southern segregationists.

By wielding the power of federal patronage, controlling the legislative calendar with surgical precision, and cultivating intimate knowledge of each senator's ambitions and vulnerabilities, Johnson achieved what [Robert Caro](https://substack.com/redirect/2d5190cf-51f0-4434-98fc-24f45f838f49?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) would later chronicle as his masterpiece: transforming a deliberative body designed for obstruction into an instrument capable of purposeful governance, all while positioning himself for the presidency he had coveted since his first Washington days as a congressional secretary in the 1930s.

**From Controlled Machines to Contested Narratives**

The connection between historical Democratic machine politics in minority precincts and Box 13 requires careful historical parsing. Urban Democratic political machines--most notably in Chicago under the [Daley family](https://substack.com/redirect/57ff285d-4008-4b69-a8fa-fa7b6dce4c10?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) and in Detroit--did exercise extraordinary influence over predominantly black precincts throughout the mid-twentieth century.

Chicago's electoral history offers instructive examples. A 1982 federal grand jury investigation documented systematic vote fraud in Chicago, where the Democratic machine maintained tight control over predominantly black South Side precincts through precinct captains who provided services in exchange for votes. The investigation revealed how election judges in majority-black precincts were pressured to inflate Democratic vote totals while suppressing Republican support. Richard Daley Sr.'s machine famously delivered massive margins for Democratic presidential candidates from Kennedy through Humphrey.

The critical distinction between these historical practices and modern critiques concerns methodology. The urban machines of the mid-twentieth century relied on in-person manipulation--ballot stuffing, repeat voting, and manipulated counting--within physical polling locations. Drop boxes, introduced more recently, operate under different procedural frameworks with varying levels of bipartisan observation and chain-of-custody documentation.

**The Voting Rights Act and Political Realignment**

The Voting Rights Act of 1965, and its attempted codification in the **'[John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act'](https://substack.com/redirect/a2c23893-5177-4337-b606-af3fc1c96524?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) of 2025 (see below) named after civil rights activist John Lewis, fundamentally transformed American democracy and party alignments. By eliminating literacy tests, poll taxes, and other [Jim Crow restrictions](https://substack.com/redirect/a7c3b235-cf8f-4405-af90-f3d6ed329d33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) while authorizing federal examiners to register voters in discriminatory counties, the VRA enfranchised millions of African Americans who had been systematically excluded from electoral participation.

The immediate electoral impacts were dramatic. A quarter-million new black voters registered in 1965 alone. By 1968, black turnout in Mississippi skyrocketed from 6.7 percent to over 60 percent. This enfranchisement simultaneously achieved Johnson's prediction (civic inclusion for black Americans) and the historical inverse of MacMillan's attributed remark--rather than simple Democratic loyalty, newly enfranchised black voters demonstrated diverse preferences, though they did trend Democratic.

The Republican Party's subsequent *"Southern Strategy" (see inset) represented the political transformation Johnson anticipated. As black voters increasingly supported Democrats, white Southern conservatives migrated to the GOP, eventually making the South a Republican stronghold--a realignment that took approximately 40 years to complete.

The nexus between LBJ, the Box 13 scandal, and the politics of black voting requires nuanced historical analysis. Johnson's proven willingness to engage in electoral fraud in 1948, combined with his documented use of racial slurs and crude political calculations, creates a portrait of a politician who viewed voting systems as instruments of power to be manipulated. The contested "200 years" quotation aligns with this documented character, even if its specific provenance remains unconfirmed.

What emerged from the Voting Rights Act was not a monolithic Democratic voting bloc controlled through fraud, but rather the legitimate political incorporation of millions of citizens long denied fundamental rights. The transformation of the Solid South from Democratic--achieved partly through fraud and suppression--to genuinely competitive and now predominantly Republican, demonstrates that electoral systems evolve alongside the demographic and ideological preferences they channel.

*The "Southern Strategy" was the Republican Party's calculated effort to dismantle the Democratic "Solid South"--a century-old political alignment born of Reconstruction-era racial animosity--and transform white Southern voters into the GOP's electoral base. Though Richard Nixon did not originate this realignment (elements appeared in Barry Goldwater's 1964 campaign), he refined it into a durable governing coalition through coded racial appeals, cultural conservatism, and strategic policy positioning that exploited the fractures LBJ had anticipated when signing civil rights legislation.
**The Architecture of the Strategy**

Nixon's approach, masterminded by strategist Kevin Phillips in 1968 and executed through surrogate campaigns and targeted rhetoric, relied on what Phillips termed "positive polarization"--deliberately alienating black voters to consolidate white support. Rather than explicit segregationist rhetoric (which Alabama Governor George Wallace employed in his independent 1968 bid), Nixon utilized "dog whistles": appeals to "states' rights," "law and order," opposition to forced busing for school integration, and criticism of the Supreme Court's activist decisions. His 1968 campaign presented the South with what Wallace could not--a viable vehicle for expressing racial and cultural grievances within the two-party system.

---|---|---
The strategy's mechanics operated on multiple levels. Nixon's 1972 reelection campaign, having learned from Wallace's success, pursued a "Southern Strategy Plus" that absorbed the Wallace constituency into the GOP fold. Campaign promises of "strict constructionist" judicial appointments--meaning judges skeptical of civil rights enforcement and affirmative action--resonated with white professionals uncomfortable with rapid social change. The administration's "Philadelphia Plan" for affirmative action, paradoxically implemented to divide unionized white workers from their black counterparts, also served strategic electoral purposes by heightening racial tension within the Democratic coalition.

**Factors Enabling Success**

The Collapse of the Jim Crow Consensus: The Civil Rights Act of 1964 and Voting Rights Act of 1965 bifurcated the Democratic Party's traditional coalition. As millions of African Americans entered the electorate and the Democratic Party embraced their cause, white Southern Democrats--who had prioritized segregation over economic populism for generations--found themselves politically homeless. The 1964 Republican National Convention, where Goldwater delegates rejected a civil rights platform plank and the Arizona senator carried five Deep South states against the Texan Johnson, demonstrated that another political home existed.

The Wallace Interlude as Market Research: George Wallace's 1968 presidential campaign, winning 46 electoral votes across the Deep South with explicitly white-supremacist appeals, proved the viability of racialized politics while establishing the ceiling of third-party segregationist politics. Nixon's strategists recognized that Wallace had demonstrated demand; their task was to supply it through the two-party structure. By 1972, Wallace had been shot, and Nixon successfully absorbed his constituency through calculated cultural positioning.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0dfb3c33-1b57-4a57-b9d9-469de39a59cc?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Suburbanization and Class Transformation: The post-war South underwent dramatic economic development and suburban expansion, creating a new class of white-collar professionals and suburban homeowners who prioritized low taxes, property rights, and neighborhood "stability" over the economic populism that had bound their agrarian ancestors to the Democratic Party. These voters responded to Nixon's "silent majority" messaging better than to Wallace's raw demagoguery.

The Weakness of Democratic Machinery: As the Voting Rights Act enfranchised black voters, urban Democratic machines that had previously controlled black precincts through patronage lost their monopoly on mobilization. Simultaneously, national Democratic candidates championing civil rights alienated white Southern county-party organizations, leaving local infrastructure vulnerable to Republican infiltration.

Court-Packing Promises: Nixon's 1968 pledge to nominate Supreme Court justices who would exercise "judicial restraint"--interpreted across the South as opposition to school integration, fair housing enforcement, and criminal justice reform--offered white voters a mechanism for resisting federal civil rights mandates without resorting to Wallace's overt defiance.

The strategy's success manifested in the 1972 electoral map, where Nixon carried every Southern state and achieved the Republican breakthrough that had eluded Goldwater. By 1980, Ronald Reagan would launch his campaign in Philadelphia, Mississippi--site of the 1964 civil rights workers' murders--with an explicit "states' rights" address, confirming the transformation of the South into the GOP's regional stronghold that has persisted for over fifty years.

**A note on The [John Lewis Voting Rights Advancement Act](https://substack.com/redirect/412171ff-358b-4984-b563-13cb0a110d64?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), introduced in 2021 and championed by Democrats through the 117th and 118th Congresses, represented a legislative response to the Supreme Court's dismantling of the Voting Rights Act's preclearance regime in '[Shelby County v. Holder](https://substack.com/redirect/4f599506-896a-4de5-8cc1-b469e28773ee?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)'. The bill, which passed the House but languished in the Senate for five years--blocked repeatedly by Republican filibusters--sought to establish a new coverage formula for federal preclearance and, controversially, to codify standards for drawing majority-minority congressional districts that critics argued would effectively mandate racial gerrymandering as a matter of federal law.

Its provisions would have required states to draw districts specifically configured to ensure minority communities could elect "candidates of their choice," a standard that opponents argue transformed race into the predominant factor in redistricting, privileging demographic sorting over traditional criteria like geographic compactness and respect for municipal boundaries.

The Act's supporters viewed these provisions as necessary protections against vote dilution; its detractors saw them as institutionalizing the very practice--drawing lines based primarily on race--that the Fourteenth and Fifteenth Amendments prohibit. On April 29, 2026, the Supreme Court effectively extinguished this legislative approach in '[Louisiana v. Callais](https://substack.com/redirect/f66f8602-8b71-40ef-9413-c1412615bc9f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)', ruling 6-3 that Louisiana's creation of a second majority-Black congressional district constituted unconstitutional racial gerrymandering. The Court's majority, reversing the logic that had governed redistricting since '[Thornburg v. Gingles'](https://substack.com/redirect/7949d498-4749-4a1a-977b-f1b5f69783a3?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (1986), held that intentional efforts to create majority-minority districts violate the Fifteenth Amendment when race predominates over traditional districting principles--a decision that rendered the John Lewis Act's core provisions constitutionally untenable while completing the jurisprudential transformation from '[Allen v. Milligan''s](https://substack.com/redirect/ee98556e-25d0-4f63-bd71-47999801a582?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) (2023) tentative preservation of minority representation to a new regime where states may now invoke "partisan" considerations to justify maps that minimize minority electoral influence, provided they do not explicitly acknowledge race as the motivating factor
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/25d1ee46-56a0-4b6f-bc2e-e2a48bd15a4e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

Peter, it's Becca. **This week, I watched the video from Biddeford, Maine.** A 26-year-old man was shot and killed by an ICE agent—an indefensible loss of life made even more staggering by the fact that he was not the person they were there to find. The agents were not wearing body cameras. ICE has offered conflicting explanations. Another man is dead, another family is grieving, and once again, the people responsible are asking us to simply trust their version of events. **Where is the accountability? Where is the outrage from my colleagues?** And where is the line that finally makes every member of Congress stand up and say: **ENOUGH IS ENOUGH.** I wish I could tell you that everyone in Congress was demanding answers right now. They are not. Too many are choosing silence, and I refuse to join them. [_**If you believe we need leaders who will speak up, demand accountability, and refuse to look away when our government takes a life, will you click here and chip in today to help me keep raising my voice?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135309585/633815887/1803060737?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZGFhNjY1YS01NjgwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=UOileSqjKD21WO7hUTZ-rM_ZEqjbocG19YLX3qY013k=) **[STAND WITH ME TODAY](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135309586/633815888/1803060737?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZGFhNjY1YS01NjgwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=UOileSqjKD21WO7hUTZ-rM_ZEqjbocG19YLX3qY013k=)** I keep returning to the same question:_Is this really the kind of country we want to live in?_ A country where federal agents can operate with enormous power and almost no transparency? Where someone can be shot inside a vehicle by agents who were not even looking for him? Where our taxpayer dollars fund brutality while members of Congress sit on their hands and wait for the news cycle to change? **I refuse to accept this as normal. Because it’s NOT.** I have traveled to communities shaken by ICE violence to demand answers. I have voted against sending more money to an agency that has repeatedly abused its power. I have pushed for oversight and accountability while too many people in Washington have remained painfully, shamefully silent. **And you can bet that I will continue doing everything within my power to stop this.** I also want to be honest with you here. Asking for a campaign contribution in the middle of so much grief can feel uncomfortable. It certainly feels uncomfortable to me, too. But the people enabling this cruelty are counting on that discomfort. They are counting on decent people becoming too exhausted, too overwhelmed, or too heartbroken to keep fighting back. They are counting on our silence. **And I cannot give them that. This campaign is the support system that allows me to keep showing up, keep speaking out, and keep putting myself on the line when silence would be easier. It helps us defend this seat, sustain our organizing, and build the political power necessary to abolish ICE and hold the Trump administration accountable.** [_**So I am asking today: If you are able, will you contribute $5, $10, $25, or whatever makes sense for you today?**_](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135309587/633815889/1803060737?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZGFhNjY1YS01NjgwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=UOileSqjKD21WO7hUTZ-rM_ZEqjbocG19YLX3qY013k=) _Help me show them that we will not become numb. We will not surrender our humanity. And we will not look away._ **[I WILL NOT LOOK AWAY](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135309588/633815890/1803060737?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMTAvMS84MTM0MiIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJkZGFhNjY1YS01NjgwLWYxMTEtYjMzNy0wMDBkM2ExNTU4Y2UiLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=UOileSqjKD21WO7hUTZ-rM_ZEqjbocG19YLX3qY013k=)** My heart is with the family and loved ones of the man who was killed. They deserve the truth, and a government that recognizes the humanity of every person whose life hangs in the balance. **Speak up. Speak out. Do what you can. And please know that I will keep doing the same.** With courage, kindness, and resolve, — Becca

A 26-year-old man was shot and killed by an ICE agent—an indefensible loss of life made even more staggering by the fact that he was not the person they were there to find. The agents were not wearing body cameras. ICE has offered conflicting explanations. Another man is dead, another family is grieving, and once again, the people responsible are asking us to simply trust their version of events. Where is the accountability? Where is the outrage from my colleagues? And where is the line that finally makes every member of Congress stand up and say: ENOUGH IS ENOUGH. [ stdin# ]Josh Shapiro for Pennsylvania
Derek, we want to
make sure you saw this:

Yesterday, MAGA Republican Stacy Garrity held an event with Ron DeSantis
on the topic of “affordability” — and VIP tickets cost up to $25,000.

Does that sound like "affordability" to you? We didn’t think so.

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/4491?t=1001&akid=144%2E245147%2EEp1n_b ]It’s clear,
Derek: Stacy Garrity is
out-of-touch with the needs of working PA families. Will you pitch in
today to make sure she doesn’t get elected the next Governor of
Pennsylvania?

[ https://act.joshshapiro.org/go/4491?t=1002&akid=144%2E245147%2EEp1n_b ]Donate →

This isn’t the first time that Garrity has demonstrated how disconnected
she is with Pennsylvania voters. When Donald Trump came to town, she stood
proudly beside him.

Seriously? The disastrous economic agenda crafted by the guy who thinks
affordability is “a fake word” and rated the economy an
“A-plus-plus-plus-plus-plus”?

If that’s not out-of-touch,
Derek, we don’t know what is.

Here’s the deal: There’s only one reason Stacy Garrity is standing proudly
next to folks like Donald Trump and Ron DeSantis — because she knows it
will bring in some serious cash from National Republicans that she can use
to spend against Josh Shapiro and everything he stands for.

your donation today gives us the

With our next mid-month fundraising deadline TONIGHT at midnight, can we

# PRESS RELEASE

**FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE**
July 15, 2026

**CONTACT**
Todd Cheewing
Todd@Ascent-Strategic.com
**LILY HAS RAISED MORE THAN ANY NH CD-02 CANDIDATE SINCE BASS**

_WILLIAMS POSTS STRONG Q2 FUNDRAISING, TOPPING $664,000 CASH ON HAND_
WEARE, N.H. — Lily Tang Williams' campaign announced another strong fundraising quarter, reporting $230k raised during the second quarter of 2026 and finishing the reporting period with $664k cash on hand, according to the campaign's July Federal Election Commission filing. The campaign has now raised $1.117 million with nearly $1 million from individual supporters during the election cycle, demonstrating continued grassroots enthusiasm and momentum as voters across New Hampshire's Second Congressional District rally behind Lily's message of freedom, fiscal responsibility, and accountable government. These figures also make it so Lily has raised more cash than any previous GOP CD-02 candidate at this point in the election cycle — since Congressman Charlie Bass was in office. The milestone speaks to Lily’s uniqueness as a candidate and her steadfastness in this race. "Our campaign continues to build because Granite Staters know Washington isn't working for them," said Lily Tang Williams. "Every contribution represents someone who believes our country can do better. I'm honored by the trust our supporters have placed in this campaign, and we're putting every dollar to work talking directly to voters across the district." The campaign's grassroots fundraising success positions Lily strongly heading into the next phase of the election, providing the resources necessary to go head-to-head with DC-insider Congresswoman Maggie Goodlander. "Lily continues to demonstrate that she has the organization, the support from ordinary Granite Staters, and the financial resources to run a highly competitive campaign," said General Consultant Michael Biundo. "These numbers reflect a campaign that is growing stronger every quarter and a candidate who is connecting with voters across the district. This is also a campaign that is fiscally responsible, managing its resources through a strong cash-on-hand figure. It’s emblematic of how Lily will treat Americans’ tax dollars in Congress.”

**About Lily Tang Williams**
Born in China just before Mao’s Cultural Revolution to working-class parents, Lily Tang Williams immigrated to the United States with nothing and built a life as an entrepreneur, educator, and community leader in Weare, NH. A living embodiment of the American Dream, she brings a uniquely powerful perspective to the fight for freedom and limited government.

In 2024, Williams won the Republican nomination and captured 47% of the general election vote against current incumbent Maggie Goodlander — coming closer than any Republican has in more than a decade to flipping NH-02. She is back and running stronger than ever in 2026.

Hi team,
This week I checked out the 4-H program's steer and dairy beef show at the Lycoming County Fair.
Take this as your regular reminder to support our local farmers.
Family-owned farms are central to Pennsylvania's identity. But they're hitting tough times right now.
The cost of everything from fertilizer to diesel to equipment repairs just keeps rising. And while big farms can weather the storm, it's increasingly difficult for small farms to make the math work. A new generation of farmers is coming up, but the current one is struggling to stay afloat. And that's bad news for our state.
And then there's the looming threat of data centers. I talked to farmers this week about how an incoming data center is threatening their livelihoods. They should not be shouldering the costs for Big Tech. Our local communities deserve a say in what happens here - not big corporations or big government.
**We need real, long-term solutions that remove obstacles for farmers and make it possible for them to continue to grow our food right here in Pennsylvania.**
That means fighting monopolies in industries like fertilizer, seeds, and meatpacking. Protecting small and mid-sized farmers from multinational corporations trying to buy our land and resources. Making it easier for farmers to work on their own equipment by supporting Right to Repair laws. Updating outdated laws that keep our farmers from being profitable and supporting new ones that lower costs.
In other words - some common sense. That's all our farmers are asking for.
Our small family farmers are doing the work that sustains all of us. I'm fighting for them to have a fair shot. And I hope you will too.
**[You can chip in to support my campaign here.](https://substack.com/redirect/2fe79936-51b9-443e-80ac-5c1528e67f81?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
But I also hope you'll take it a step further. Buy from a local farm. Seek out local dairy. And check out the county fair in Lycoming. You don't want to miss it.
Thank you,
Rachel Wallace

The collapsed buildings, the death toll, the rescue teams pulling survivors from the rubble, **the world watched, then largely moved on.** But for the children left behind, the danger didn't end when the ground stopped shaking. **In some ways, it was only the beginning.** Displacement does something traffickers understand better than almost anyone. It breaks the systems that normally protect a child -- records, schools, familiar faces, parents who never let go of their hand. In that broken space, a stranger offering "help," a ride, a promise of safety somewhere else, can be all it takes for a child to disappear.

I've sat with survivors. I've heard what it costs a family to lose a child this way, and what it takes to bring one home. And I've learned that disasters like the one in Venezuela don't create new evil, they simply hand existing evil an opening it has used again and again. If this is the first time you're hearing from me, my name is Eduardo Verastegui, and I produced the film Sound of Freedom. The film Sound of Freedom was truly a movie that launched a movement. That movement is now. Our mission at the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** is to **stop the sale of God's children.** We do that through five pillars:
---
* **Prevention**
* **Intervention**
* **Education**
* **Information**
* **Influence**

---
We are working urgently, with trusted partners on the ground, to:
---
* Find children who have already fallen into trafficking, including exploitation happening online in the chaos of the disaster.
* Support rescue operations that bring a child out of danger and into safety.
* Provide a safe bed the moment a child is free.
* Fund reunification when a family can be found and verified.
* Walk alongside a child through long-term care when there is nowhere safe to send them yet.

clean_body: The earthquake is over. The hunt for children has begun. After the earthquakes in Venezuela, traffickers are already moving. Here's how we're responding. | | | | | | | | GOD'S CHILDREN ARE NOT FOR SALE | | | | Friend, The earthquakes in Venezuela dominated the news for a matter of days. The collapsed buildings, the death toll, the rescue teams pulling survivors from the rubble, the world watched, then largely moved on. But for the children left behind, the danger didn't end when the ground stopped shaking. In some ways, it was only the beginning. Displacement does something traffickers understand better than almost anyone. It breaks the systems that normally protect a child -- records, schools, familiar faces, parents who never let go of their hand. In that broken space, a stranger offering "help," a ride, a promise of safety somewhere else, can be all it takes for a child to disappear. We've set an urgent goal to raise $50,000 in the next 30 days to help rescue children, provide safe shelter, and reunite families before more children disappear into trafficking. Every gift brings us one step closer.Will you help us reach this lifesaving goal today? I've sat with survivors. I've heard what it costs a family to lose a child this way, and what it takes to bring one home. And I've learned that disasters like the one in Venezuela don't create new evil, they simply hand existing evil an opening it has used again and again. If this is the first time you're hearing from me, my name is Eduardo Verastegui, and I produced the film Sound of Freedom. The film Sound of Freedom was truly a movie that launched a movement. That movement is now. Our mission at the Sound of Freedom Foundation is to stop the sale of God's children. We do that through five pillars: Prevention Intervention Education Information Influence We are working urgently, with trusted partners on the ground, to: Find children who have already fallen into trafficking, including exploitation happening online in the chaos of the disaster. Support rescue operations that bring a child out of danger and into safety. Provide a safe bed the moment a child is free. Fund reunification when a family can be found and verified. Walk alongside a child through long-term care when there is nowhere safe to send them yet. "Defend the weak and the fatherless; uphold the cause of the poor and the oppressed. Rescue the weak and the needy; deliver them from the hand of the wicked." (Psalm 82:3-4) That command is what guides every decision this Foundation makes. It is not a suggestion. It is not poetry. It is an instruction, and I take it as one. We're trusting God to help us raise $50,000 in the next 30 days, but He often answers prayers through people willing to act. I hope you'll be one of them today. Friend, I am asking you urgently, humbly, and personally to make your first gift today. Please do not wait. For God's children, Eduardo Verastegui Sound of Freedom, Producer For the Sound of Freedom Foundation P.S. Right now, a displaced child in Venezuela is being watched by someone who does not have their best interest at heart. Your gift today helps make sure someone who does gets there first. 6671 Southwest Freeway, Suite 700, Houston TX 77074

| | **CONROY RAISES $600,000 IN SECOND QUARTER**
_Strong Fundraising, Recent Supreme Court Ruling Sets Stage for Fair Fight in OH-01_

---
| |

CINCINNATI, OH — Eric Conroy, the Republican nominee in Ohio's 1st Congressional District, announced today that his campaign raised more than $600,000 in the second quarter of 2026, bringing his campaign to date total to $1,400,000 with four months to go:
The record quarter caps a stretch of building strength for Conroy, a former CIA Case Officer and Air Force intelligence officer who won the May primary in dominant fashion and carries endorsements from President Trump, Vice President Vance, Speaker Mike Johnson, and Ohio's Republican leadership into the general election against Democrat Greg Landsman.
_“Voters in Southwest Ohio are ready for a change, and they're putting their money where their votes will be in November,”_ **said Conroy.** _“Greg Landsman has spent four years in Washington voting with the extremists in his party and delivering nothing for this district. We're building the resources, the ground game, and the coalition to retire him. This is just the start. We will return commonsense leadership for southwest Ohio in Congress.”_
The financial picture in OH-01 has shifted sharply in Conroy's favor. Conroy’s strong fundraising coupled with the U.S. Supreme Court's June 30 decision striking down limits on coordinated party spending means national Republicans can now invest directly alongside the campaign — helping to even the financial playing field against an incumbent in Landsman who’s spent four years doing favors to lobbyists and collecting DC pac and special interest money. The Congressional Leadership Fund has already reserved $4 million in Cincinnati airtime this fall to support Conroy, a clear signal that Republicans see OH-01 as one of the best pickup opportunities in the country.
Redistricting moved Ohio's 1st District to R+3, and national handicappers rate the race a toss-up. Landsman now has to defend a record that doesn't match his district — and for the first time, he'll face a challenger with the resources to make sure every voter knows it.
###

🏆TODAY: Powered by One Cup Community Call | | | **Peter -****The World Cup reminded us how far underdogs can go when they refuse to give up.** This summer, we watched teams the world counted out rewrite history. **The stories that inspired us during the World Cup are about what happens when people who have been underestimated, under-resourced, and counted out refuse to give up.** Cape Verde's goalkeeper, Vozinha, spent years working as a bus driver and electrician before becoming a professional player. At 40 years old, he helped his country advance in its first-ever World Cup. His mother almost missed watching him play because new visa bond requirements made it impossible for her to travel—until public pressure changed that. Paraguay's Orlando Gill once sold his own national team jersey to pay his newborn son's hospital bills. This summer, his saves carried Paraguay into the Round of 16. clean_body: 🏆TODAY: Powered by One Cup Community Call | | | Peter -The World Cup reminded us how far underdogs can go when they refuse to give up. This summer, we watched teams the world counted out rewrite history. The stories that inspired us during the World Cup are about what happens when people who have been underestimated, under-resourced, and counted out refuse to give up. Cape Verde's goalkeeper, Vozinha, spent years working as a bus driver and electrician before becoming a professional player. At 40 years old, he helped his country advance in its first-ever World Cup. His mother almost missed watching him play because new visa bond requirements made it impossible for her to travel—until public pressure changed that. Paraguay's Orlando Gill once sold his own national team jersey to pay his newborn son's hospital bills. This summer, his saves carried Paraguay into the Round of 16. These stories remind us of something bigger than sports. Our communities are stronger because of people from every corner of the world. The same diversity that makes the World Cup unforgettable makes our country stronger every single day. But we can't truly celebrate the people who enrich our communities while millions of immigrants continue to live without safety, dignity, or a pathway to citizenship. ****Together, we'll explore what this World Cup teaches us about the power of diversity, resilience, and collective action—and what it will take to build a country where everyone can live with safety, dignity, and a pathway to citizenship. You'll hear stories that connect the tournament to our movement, learn how attacks on immigrant communities affect all of us, and discover ways you can take action alongside people who believe our communities are strongest when everyone belongs. Movements win because ordinary people keep showing up for one another. That's how underdogs change history. That's how we build a country where every family can thrive. These tragedies mark a violent surge of deadly immigration enforcement across the country as the Administration expands workplace immigration raids and enforcement on the streets of cities nationwide. The legacy immigrant fathers like Lorenzo and Johan leave behind is defined not by their status, but by the love they showed to the people around them. **Many of us know all too well the story of our immigrant parents and neighbors who never complain about the grueling days of work ahead, whose hands are marked by callouses one can only get from 30 years of building homes in our neighborhoods, and who raise their families with the value of hard work**. Many of us know all too well the story of our immigrant parents and neighbors who never complain about the grueling days of work ahead, whose hands are marked by callouses one can only get from 30 years of building homes in our neighborhoods, and who raise their families with the value of hard work. But we also know the story of our immigrant parents and workers in America whose lives are increasingly treated as disposable. These tragedies, and so many more, have taken place as the country celebrates the diversity, resilience, and strength of immigrants that have made this World Cup a success. We cannot claim to value the joy immigrants bring to our country, while simultaneously denying them the basic safety and stability they need. Our communities are stronger because of people from every corner of the world. The same diversity that has made this World Cup unforgettable makes our country stronger every single day. Together, we'll explore what this World Cup teaches us about the power of diversity, resilience, and collective action—and what it will take to build a country where everyone can live with safety, dignity, and citizenship. ********** The legacy left behind by Lorenzo, Johan, and so many others who have been killed by agents in the streets or died in detention camps hundreds of miles from their families is not defined by their status, but by the love they showed to the people around them. Through constant sacrifice, quiet generosity, and selfless service that made our communities better. We must carry forward their legacy. Although this moment feels daunting, we must remember that movements win because ordinary people keep showing up for one another. That's how underdogs change history. The stories that inspired us the most during the World Cup are the ones of the players who have been underestimated, under-resourced, and counted out, and yet refused to give up. Cape Verde's goalkeeper, Vozinha, spent years working as a bus driver and electrician before becoming a professional player. At 40 years old, he helped his country advance in its first-ever World Cup. His mother almost missed watching him play because of new visa requirements - but public pressure changed that. Paraguay's goalkeeper Orlando Gill once had to sell his own national team jersey to pay his newborn son's hospital bills. This summer, his saves carried Paraguay into the Round of 16. These stories remind us that when ordinary people keep showing up for one another, that's how WE will build a country where everyone has the resources they need to thrive. ** In unity, Matias and the UWD team | Follow us on: | | | | |

# **Trump orders ICE to resume vehicle stops after brief pause**
President Donald Trump **[directed ICE to resume vehicle stops](https://substack.com/redirect/28308c78-9ab7-4057-91ed-ee943ba37cb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** Wednesday morning via Truth Social, reversing a brief internal pause triggered by two recent deadly shootings involving agents pulling over vehicles in Texas and Maine. **We secured a MAJOR victory for freedom in New Hampshire, and it’s all because of grassroots patriots like YOU who refused to stay silent!**

Governor Kelly Ayotte has officially signed House Bill 1268 into law, delivering a major victory for parental rights and education freedom in the Live Free or Die State.

| | **House Bill 1268 restores parents as the rightful leaders of their children's education.**

The new law makes initial notifications and annual evaluations optional, ends heavy-handed district micromanagement, and protects homeschooling families from having paperwork used against them in truancy or welfare cases.

By removing unnecessary bureaucracy while keeping sensible accountability, this law **trusts parents to know what is best for their own children.**

This is a significant victory for education freedom and another reminder that **parents, not government bureaucrats,** should be making decisions about their children's education.

We also thank Governor Kelly Ayotte for signing House Bill 1268 into law and standing with New Hampshire families. Her signature has helped make New Hampshire a national leader for homeschooling freedom and parental rights.

**This victory belongs to every citizen who made a phone call, sent an email, and stood with us in defense of freedom.**

With your support, we proved once again that when engaged citizens speak up, good policy can prevail.

For New Hampshire,

| | Lifе and death Son of Mykhailo Sulyma, Ivan came from a petty noble (szlachta) family. He was born in Rohoshchi (next to Chernihiv). He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw

Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

name: Roy Cooper (via Cooper Victory Fund)
subject: This decision wasn’t easy to make
body:
This race is too consequential to sit out. The stakes are too high.
|
# [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/6532?source=&t=1&akid=2114%2E124072%2EXVGHeM)
| | | |
---
Peter, deciding to run for this U.S. Senate seat wasn’t easy.
I had planned on serving North Carolina from here at home. That’s why I was so humbled when North Carolinians twice elected me to be their Governor.
**But this Senate race is too consequential to sit out. The stakes are simply too high.**
I entered this race to fight for people like you, who’ve put your trust in me – and I have full faith that together, we can win. But tonight, we’re facing a crucial test of our grassroots movement’s strength:
At 11:59 p.m., our mid-month deadline will come to a close. [**_So with time running out to reach our ambitious $750,000 goal, I’m personally asking you to help out by making your first $5 donation, right now._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk768&amount=5&t=8&akid=2114%2E124072%2EXVGHeM)
| | [DONATE](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk768&amount=5&t=9&akid=2114%2E124072%2EXVGHeM)
---
I’m running because our nation cannot afford two more years of unchecked Republican power in Washington. The attacks on health care, on democratic values and even on Americans – **they have to stop.**
Our leaders should be focusing on strengthening our communities by investing in public schools, securing health care access and prioritizing hardworking folks over the wealthiest few. That’s what I strove to do in North Carolina – and by the end of my time in office, we added thousands of jobs by expanding the clean energy economy, gave public school teachers statewide a much-needed raise, expanded Medicaid and more.
**This is the work I’m ready to continue as the next Senator from North Carolina. That means we have to flip this seat from red to blue for the first time in a generation and take back the Senate for the people who elect us, which is easier said than done.**
I’ve never lost a race, but this one will be the most competitive of my career. It’s the best pick-up opportunity for Democrats this cycle, and our ability to flip the Senate hinges on us succeeding. That’s why far-right groups are already spending nearly $100 million so far to attack me – and experts expect this to be the most expensive Senate race ever, so they will spare no expense to help President Trump’s handpicked candidate buy his way to victory.
So if they see us missing goals like the one we set for tonight, they _will_ use this as an opportunity to strike. They _will_ flood the airwaves with millions more in attack ads to smear me, knowing that their investments are working as intended, because we _will not_ have enough funds to fight back.
[**_Chipping in $5, $25 or whatever amount is right for you before the end of the day won’t just help us close the gap in time; it’ll prove to everyone that momentum is on our side. So if you’re with us, Peter, please make it clear by making a donation right away._**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk768&amount=5&t=10&akid=2114%2E124072%2EXVGHeM)

Roy Cooper

Democrat Roy Cooper is running for U.S. Senate to help take back the Majority for Democrats. North Carolina is Democrats’ best chance to flip a seat from red to blue — the path to stopping Republicans in Washington starts here.

National Republicans will target North Carolina as a key battleground and invest heavily in defeating us.

Cooper is a former state legislator, Attorney General, and most recently Governor of North Carolina. North Carolina will be the most competitive Senate election of 2026, and Cooper enters the race as the most formidable candidate of either party.

Cooper’s signature achievements include helping to expand Medicaid and helping make NC the top state for business by creating thousands of jobs and growing the clean energy economy.

| | | | | |
# This Week with Team Berge
Hi Team Berge,
There are plenty of ways to help move this campaign forward this week from welcoming neighbors at community events to knocking doors and spreading the word online.
Every conversation helps introduce more voters to Emily and the community-focused campaign we are building across Wisconsin’s 3rd Congressional District. Take a look at the opportunities below and choose the one that works best for you.
**Have a question about an event or how to get involved? Just reply to this email and we will help get you connected!**
---
| |
# Featured Event: Boogie with Berge!
---
| | | | | | | | | | |
---
| | |

Please come join us for Boogie with Berge, a free, high-energy evening of music, dancing, and community at The Plus in Eau Claire! Come enjoy live music, connect with other supporters, and help us build momentum as we get out the vote for Emily. RSVP below!

---
| [RSVP](https://us.list-manage.com/16SNrBzzPaA?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)
---
| |
# Upcoming Volunteer Opportunities

Community events, parades, meet and greets, and local gatherings give us valuable opportunities to connect with voters where they live.
Volunteers make these appearances possible. Depending on the event, you may help greet attendees, hand out campaign materials, take photos, assist with sign-in, walk in a parade, or simply show your support by wearing your Berge shirt or button.
**Friday, July 17**(5:00pm-8:00pm) - Eau Claire Meet & Greet**Saturday, July 18**(11:00am-2:00pm) - Portage County Fair of Amherst Parade**Saturday, July 18**(11:00am-1:00pm) - Eau Claire Post Card Writing**Sunday, July 19**(10:30am-1:00pm) - Cazenovia Celebration Parade**Monday, July 20**(3:00pm-5:00pm) - Eau Claire Post Card Writing**Tuesday, July 21**(5:00pm-7:00pm) - Eau Claire Post Card Writing**Wednesday, July 22**(5:00pm-7:00pm) - La Crosse Meet & Greet**Sunday, July 26**(11:00am-1:00pm) - Richland Center Meet & Greet**Tuesday, July 28**(6:00pm-8:00pm) - Farmers Union Town Hall**Thursday, July 30**(5:00pm-8:00pm) - Boogie with Berge!
---
| | | | | | | | | | | [Sign Up to Volunteer](https://us.list-manage.com/KsUBjTGaj4X?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)
---
| |
# Canvassing Opportunities
---
| |

Some of the most important campaign moments happen one conversation at a time. Canvassing, phone banking, texting, and postcard writing allow us to personally connect with voters throughout the district. No previous experience is necessary. Our team will provide the training, materials, and support you need to feel comfortable getting started.
**Saturday, July 18**(11:00am) - Knock doors in Eau Claire**Saturday, July 18**(10:00am) - Knock doors in Stevens Point**Saturday, July 18**(11:00am) - Knock doors in La Crosse**Thursday, July 23**(12:00pm-2:00pm) - Knock doors in La Crosse**Thursday, July 30**(12:00pm-2:00pm) - Knock doors in La CrosseWant to canvass in your own community, phone bank, or send postcards? You don’t need to be an expert to get started. We will make sure you have everything you need and are trained, just use this [Canvassing Form](https://us.list-manage.com/13ul5uyyS7W?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1) and we will get back to you shortly.
---
| [Join a Canvass Launch](https://us.list-manage.com/IrmJ2VNJt1y?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)
---
| |
# Support the Campaign from Anywhere
---
| |

Can’t attend an event this week? There are still several easy ways to help increase Emily’s visibility and reach more voters:
Request a Berge yard sign:[ Yard Sign Request Form](https://us.list-manage.com/bbubMGdODj7?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)Order a Berge shirt and wear it to events, parades, and around town:[ Order Your Shirt Today](https://us.list-manage.com/14llGucQ0Te?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)Submit a written testimonial about why you are supporting Emily:[ Submit a Story](https://us.list-manage.com/ppBROWQWY4A?e=1362dd258a&c2id=d51b517ba2e5c823fe0a3e4f0e8330f1)Host a postcard writing party with friends, family, or neighbors. This is a great way to help reach voters while building community.Boost social media engagement by liking, commenting on, and sharing campaign posts. Follow Berge for Congress on Facebook, Instagram, TikTok, Reddit, and Bluesky.Wear your Berge button around town. Volunteers have shared great stories about conversations started with neighbors, cashiers, servers, and community members just by wearing a button.

### SENATE UPDATE: What We're Fighting For
Over the last several months, much of my work has focused on pushing back against the abuses, corruption, and lawlessness of the Trump Administration.

Every day brings new challenges, from attacks on our democratic institutions and constitutional rights to rising costs that continue to squeeze working families. At the same time, events around the world remind us that decisions made in Washington have profound consequences both for Americans at home and many abroad.

That is certainly true of the illegal war with Iran.

Since the beginning of this conflict, I have opposed President Trump's unauthorized war of choice and pushed for Congress to reclaim its constitutional role in decisions about the use of military force. Recently, I went to the [Senate floor](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2flive%2f0_iz2dn2-as&redir_log=120377771147272) to support another War Powers Resolution aimed at preventing further escalation and helping move us away from a wider regional war.

This conflict has left the United States worse off than before it began. Fourteen American servicemembers have lost their lives, thousands of civilians have been killed or injured, and families here at home have paid the price through higher costs and economic uncertainty.

As I've said repeatedly, [when you're in a hole, stop digging](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.instagram.com%2fp%2fDZuisRuNVe8%2f&redir_log=542814300627271).

While we face these daily challenges both at home and abroad head-on, I've also been focused on another question: what comes next?

While it is important to continue fighting back against Trump's abuses of power and reckless actions, it is equally important that we continue advancing ideas that address the challenges Americans face every day. People want to know not only what we're against, but what we're for.

At its core, the challenge facing our country today is not just Donald Trump's lawlessness. It is that too many Americans rightly feel like the economy is rigged against them - [and in favor of billionaires and special interests. ](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mphhiyryw22l&redir_log=864979743236449)

Families are working harder than ever, but struggling to keep up with the cost of housing, healthcare, childcare, groceries, and electric bills. Meanwhile, some of the wealthiest corporations and individuals continue to benefit from rules that allow them to accumulate more wealth and power while everyone else treads water or falls further behind.

We need to change that. We need to take on powerful special interests, lower costs for working families, and build an economy that rewards work over wealth. That is the lens through which I'm approaching much of my work in the Senate. Here are a few of the fights I'm leading to move our country forward.
---
### A Tax Relief Plan that Puts Money Back in Working Americans' Pockets, Paid for with a Surtax on Millionaires
Across the country, millions of Americans are working hard every day for their paychecks but are still struggling to make ends meet. Families are being squeezed by rising costs - from groceries and housing to health care and childcare - and too many people simply do not have enough income to cover those basic expenses.

I understand that challenge, and [I have a plan](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-kelly-gillibrand-booker-kim-beyer-introduce-new-bill-to-cut-taxes-for-millions-of-working-americans&redir_log=115059721031145) to do something about it.

It's called the [Working Americans Tax Cut Act](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fimo%2fmedia%2fdoc%2fworking_americans_tax_cut_act_explainer.pdf&redir_log=760436808366643), legislation designed to help working people keep more of their hard-earned paychecks. The idea behind the proposal is straightforward: Americans who are earning just enough to cover their basic living expenses should not have to pay federal income tax, and workers who make just above the median cost of living should be able to keep more of the money they earn. To pay for this plan, my bill implements a millionaire surtax - requiring those making more than a million dollars annually to pay a surtax on the amount of their income over a million dollars.

If your paycheck amounts to a living wage, you should be able to live off it - not have it taxed away. Twenty Senators have joined me to cosponsor this effort.

Under this plan, over 130 million Americans would receive tax relief:
* A single worker earning $50,000 per year would typically keep about $2,500 more of their income.
* A typical family earning $95,000 per year would keep about $6,000 more of their paychecks to help cover household expenses.

This proposal addresses one side of the [affordability challenge](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mgvpyt33ps2z&redir_log=565079066024447) that many Americans are facing today. While we must continue working to lower costs, we also need to make sure families have enough income to meet those costs.

Unlike the Trump-Republican tax law - which directed nearly 75% of its benefits to those in the top 20% of incomes and almost 50% to the wealthiest 5% - our proposal focuses tax relief on those who need it. Virtually every dollar of tax relief under this plan goes to the other 80% of working Americans and middle-class families. And unlike Trump's tax law, which exploded the national debt while rewarding those at the top, this legislation is fully paid for by ensuring that the wealthiest Americans contribute more towards our shared prosperity.
### Ensuring Big Corporations, Not Consumers, Pay the Bills for Data Centers
Across Maryland and throughout the country, some of the richest corporations on the planet are rapidly building [massive data centers](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2fwatch%3fv%3dPoz7ie0ivlo%26t%3d4s&redir_log=937669627372356) that consume extraordinary amounts of electricity. Increasingly, these power-hungry facilities are driving up the electric bills of families living in the same region.

Although they are not the only factor causing electricity prices to rise, these new data centers are creating higher energy demand and new infrastructure needs, the costs of which are ultimately getting passed on to you - the consumer. Indeed, in just a few years, consumers in our region have had to pay for about $28 billion in additional costs due to data centers - including $21 billion in capacity costs and $7 billion in transmission costs. By 2028, the average household in the mid-Atlantic grid region (PJM) - the nation's largest electric grid serving 67 million Americans in 13 states, including Maryland - is projected to see their energy bills increase by $840 per year due to the increase in capacity costs alone. That does not include the added charges to consumers of higher transmission costs.

That's why I introduced the [Power for the People Act](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-leads-new-bill-to-ensure-americans-arent-footing-the-bill-for-big-data-centers&redir_log=27546672624990). My legislation would require data center developers - not working families - to pay for the infrastructure and energy costs their projects create. It would also help protect grid reliability, encourage cleaner energy development, and support good-paying, union jobs.

This is about fairness, protecting consumers, and keeping utility bills from climbing even higher, because Americans should not be forced to underwrite corporate profits. I'm working to stop that from happening and keep utility costs affordable for Maryland families.
### Addressing Climate Change and Making Polluters Pay
We're at a turning point in our fight against climate change. We're seeing rising sea levels, record temperatures, and extreme weather events. In Maryland, coastal communities along the Chesapeake Bay and the Eastern Shore are facing increasingly frequent tidal flooding. In Western Maryland, communities swung from extreme drought to devastating flash floods.

For decades, some of the largest fossil fuel companies have known about their role in driving climate change while shifting the costs onto taxpayers, communities, and future generations. Direct subsidies to the fossil fuel sector are estimated to cost American taxpayers $29.4 billion annually, while the health consequences of rising greenhouse gas emissions and climate change cost Americans more than $820 billion each year in medical bills.

Families pay the price through rising health care costs, more frequent and severe natural disasters, damage to homes and infrastructure, and the growing costs associated with climate change. Meanwhile, the companies most responsible continue to [generate enormous profits](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mlgkozucxs2l&redir_log=4572747232453).

That needs to change. That's why I introduced the [Polluters Pay Climate Fund Act](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fin-first-action-of-119th-congress-van-hollen-reintroduces-legislation-to-make-polluters-pay-for-fueling-climate-change&redir_log=015637929681199).

My legislation would require the largest fossil fuel companies - those responsible for the greatest share of carbon pollution - to contribute to a $1 trillion fund dedicated to addressing the costs of climate change. The fee only applies to the heavy hitters: fossil fuel companies responsible for at least 1 billion tons of carbon dioxide emissions between 2000 and 2022. The resources from this fund would go towards helping communities prepare for and recover from climate disasters, strengthen critical infrastructure, support the hardest-hit communities, and create good-paying jobs.

This initiative would be a big step forward in our efforts to tackle some of the worst damage from the climate crisis, because the biggest polluters should pay to help clean up the mess they caused - and those who polluted the most should pay the most, not working families.
### Moving Toward Medicare for All
We also need to confront the reality that our health care system is [failing far too many Americans](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3mpjrjm3wes2b&redir_log=179093666112448).

Families continue to face rising premiums, higher deductibles, increasing out-of-pocket costs, and barriers to accessing the care that they need. Despite spending more on health care than our peers, we continue to achieve worse health outcomes.

Devastating cuts to Medicaid and SNAP by the Trump Administration and congressional Republicans in the so-called "Big Beautiful Bill" and their failure to extend the enhanced Affordable Care Act tax credits at the beginning of this year have only made these challenges worse for Maryland families. Hundreds of thousands of Marylanders will be kicked off their health insurance or be priced out entirely because of these Trump cuts, and health care costs are increasing for everyone. At some point, we need to stop tinkering around the edges of a system that is fundamentally broken.

I have long supported universal health care. A single-payer system would reduce administrative waste, lower overall costs, and ensure that health care dollars are directed toward patients rather than excessive bureaucracy, corporate interests, and profiteering middlemen.

Health care should not depend on your income, your employer, or your ZIP code. Every Marylander, and every American, deserves access to quality, affordable health care - and that is why I support [Medicare for All](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov%2fpost%2f3m6xkwvnvlc2o&redir_log=623457000836450).
### Expanding Access to Affordable Housing
Last month, the House and Senate took an important step forward in tackling our nation's housing challenges, from increasing the supply of homes to improving access to affordable housing options. Trump may say that tackling housing costs is a "big yawn," but that couldn't be further from the truth. We have a housing crisis in this country as working Americans too often face costs they simply cannot afford. That's why I supported the bipartisan 21st Century Road to Housing Act, which will help expand housing affordability for both renters and buyers through new programs and critical reforms. But Donald Trump refused to sign this bill - which ultimately became law last week after his inaction - once again showing where his [misguided priorities](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.instagram.com%2fp%2fDZ_SfXXFGne%2f&redir_log=004646796803269) lie.

Within this legislation, I worked to ensure we're better upholding our duty to support our veterans - securing the inclusion of [two bipartisan bills](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.vanhollen.senate.gov%2fnews%2fpress-releases%2fvan-hollen-secures-senate-passage-of-bills-to-improve-homebuying-process-for-veterans&redir_log=226152077411976) I authored that will help more veterans and their families secure affordable home loans.

This package is an important first step, but there is much more to do, and I will continue to fight for affordable housing for Marylanders and for the American people.
### Thank You
The immediate task before us is clear: we must continue pushing back against the abuses, corruption, and lawlessness of the Trump Administration. But opposition alone is not enough. Marylanders, and all Americans, deserve to know what we are fighting for. We must let our fellow Americans know what we will do if we are given the chance. The initiatives outlined above are among the many measures I am pursuing, which also include more support for public education and badly overdue and desperately needed campaign finance reform.

The bottom line is that we should be fighting for an economy where work is rewarded more than wealth and a country where the doors of opportunity are open to all. We should be fighting to lower costs for working families, not cut taxes for billionaires. We should be fighting to ensure that polluters pay for the damage they cause, that powerful corporations cannot shift their costs onto consumers, and that every American has access to affordable health care.

The challenges ahead are significant, and powerful interests will oppose many of these ideas. But throughout our history, progress has come when Americans organized, spoke out, and demanded a government that works for them rather than for the wealthy and well-connected. I see many of you doing just that across Maryland, and I remain committed to being your partner in this fight.

As always, thank you for staying engaged in this work.

Onwards,
Chris Van Hollen

To see more on my daily efforts to fight back against the Trump Administration, follow me on: [YouTube](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.youtube.com%2f%40senatorvanhollen&redir_log=49030338036296), [Bluesky](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fbsky.app%2fprofile%2fvanhollen.senate.gov&redir_log=939838092693319), [Instagram](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.instagram.com%2fchrisvanhollen%3futm_source%3dig_web_button_share_sheet%26igsh%3dZDNlZDc0MzIxNw%253D%253D&redir_log=547268099313732), [Threads](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.threads.com%2f%40chrisvanhollen&redir_log=958032566321279), [Facebook](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fwww.facebook.com%2fchrisvanhollen%2f&redir_log=328155479639284), and [X](https://outreach.senate.gov/iqextranet/iqClickTrk.aspx?&cid=SenVanHollen&crop=15309.61740440.8066600.7517223&report_id=&redirect=https%3a%2f%2fx.com%2fChrisVanHollen&redir_log=218313979356198).
