# Iran and Ceasefire
* **U.S. resumes naval blockade of Iran and launches new strikes:** U.S. Central Command [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/6de8b8f9-46f9-4d89-9d67-eb88fc6b0ede?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday afternoon that American forces had resumed their naval blockade of vessels traveling to and from Iranian ports and coastal areas. An hour earlier, the U.S. launched another round of strikes on Iran, four days after it began its current, ceasefire-shattering round of strikes.
* Tuesday's U.S. strikes targeted civilian infrastructure in the country, including a wheat warehouse in Hoveyzeh and a mineral-water factory in Dehloran, according to Iranian state media.
* CENTCOM [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/e275074f-5a9c-4239-8234-8ab93cf6720b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday evening that it had completed a seven-hour wave of strikes on Iran, reporting that it hit dozens of military targets near the Strait of Hormuz and along Iran's southern coast.
* U.S. strikes hit the city of Bushehr on Wednesday, according to the region's governor, hitting four locations without causing casualties.
* Another strike on a barracks in the city of Iranshahr reportedly [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/5f173670-16ed-4e19-9c6f-3f2c6bc9cc96?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) 7 people, mostly soldiers, and wounded 15 others, according to Iran's Tasnim News Agency.
* U.S. strikes [continued](https://substack.com/redirect/3e000807-832c-4335-b8ff-768378cda197?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday morning, with one strike hitting the Iranian port city of Chabahar. CENTCOM [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/d4aa0791-badf-4c8e-a836-c0504ec4dd67?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a conclusion to a "90-minute" wave of strikes at 3:00 p.m., Tehran local time.
* U.S. strikes have [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/c5539894-3afb-4c70-be94-7078f9fffc79?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) more than 30 civilians and wounded 260 others since last week, an Iranian government spokesperson reported.
* **Iran responds, hits U.S. bases in the Gulf:** Iran launched several strikes on U.S. bases in the region in response to Washington's continued attacks.
* One attack set fire to and destroyed a U.S. military logistics and support center at Kuwait's Mina Abdullah port, Iran's military claimed, which supports a vital industrial and refining area south of Kuwait City. Footage of the site showed what appears to be an Iranian drone striking a burning warehouse. The IRGC also claimed it hit several other military targets in Kuwait, including a satellite communications center, a missile- and air-defense radar, a Patriot air-defense complex, and HIMARS launch platforms.
* Neither the U.S. nor the Kuwaiti governments have [confirmed](https://substack.com/redirect/e5b5bd0a-8c16-426f-b36e-518a02b89145?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) any damage, though Kuwait [claimed](https://substack.com/redirect/d1f5b299-a84b-40e6-9a97-5afdfeb35d25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) it had intercepted one ballistic missile, five cruise missiles, and 33 hostile drones from Iran on Tuesday evening.
* Iran also struck and [damaged](https://substack.com/redirect/d1f5b299-a84b-40e6-9a97-5afdfeb35d25?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) a Kuwaiti naval vessel, wounding four Kuwaiti soldiers, according to the Kuwaiti government, which added that the wounded were in stable condition.
* Another Iranian strike [hit](https://substack.com/redirect/883b797f-776d-467a-b46f-17ea4da38697?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the U.S. military base at Al-Azraq in Jordan on Tuesday, the IRGC claimed in a statement.
* Sirens were also [heard](https://substack.com/redirect/3b26fa28-0ffc-49f0-b9ad-33c7aa76c2ef?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Wednesday morning in Bahrain, which hosts the U.S. Navy's Fleet headquarters and which the IRGC said it struck on Tuesday.
* Separately, CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper [said](https://substack.com/redirect/e275074f-5a9c-4239-8234-8ab93cf6720b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday that Iran had attacked seven commercial ships in the past week, in attacks which he claimed killed or wounded nearly a dozen civilian crew members.
* On Wednesday morning, a cargo ship [sank](https://substack.com/redirect/9d8b66fc-2304-46f3-9480-135fe80dc327?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) in the Gulf, though the cause of the incident remains unclear. All 23 of its crew members were rescued, according to Al Jazeera.
* An unidentified drone also crashed into Iraq's Grand Faw Port, though it reportedly did not interrupt the port's operations.
* **Trump ditches calls for a 20% Hormuz fee:** In a Truth Social post on Tuesday morning, U.S. President Donald Trump [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/02fbf29a-1486-494d-b44c-d9b907f2af37?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that he would no longer be pursuing a 20% fee for all ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and that he would "replace" the non-existent fee with "Trade and Investment Deals that the various Gulf States will be making with the United States."
* In the post, Trump claimed, despite the ongoing hostilities and Iranian claims to the contrary, that the "Strait is open to ALL Ship traffic except for Iran."
* Iranian state media reported Wednesday that the Strait has become "impassable" for commercial shipping, with at least two vessels stopped by the IRGC after warning shots were fired over the past 24 hours.

* **Trump threatens strikes on additional Iranian infrastructure:** In an interview with Fox News' Trey Yingst on Tuesday, Trump [said](https://substack.com/redirect/af0dce0b-331d-4dd7-a486-8779b68cfb33?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) he would strike Iran's power plants and bridges unless Iran's leadership "gets to the table and negotiates" by next week.
* The threats follow U.S. strikes on a mineral water factory and a wheat warehouse in Iran, reported on Tuesday.
* He [asserted](https://substack.com/redirect/35a3629e-2492-49d7-93e9-5f69fe6f6cb8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) again that the Strait of Hormuz is "open if people want to go through it," though he implied otherwise by speculating on "great alternatives," "including Texas, including Alaska."
* Trump also [told](https://substack.com/redirect/6d827f94-85f6-4953-aa8e-63ff8fbc115c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Yingst that a ground invasion of Iran's Kharg Island, the vital hub for about 90 percent of the country's oil exports, is "unlikely" for now, though he might reconsider this "if we degrade them far enough and deep enough back."
* **IRGC says there will be "energy for everyone or no one": **In [response](https://substack.com/redirect/85a284a3-0590-4052-b1d1-31610104e028?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to the resumption of the U.S. blockade, the IRGC threatened on Wednesday to prevent all oil exports from the Gulf, saying in a statement, "the export of oil and gas from the region will be either for everyone or for no one."
* **More than 200 vessels ask Iran for permission to transit the Strait, PGSA says:** More than 200 non-Iranian vessels [sought](https://substack.com/redirect/0332b3d8-2654-4703-a50e-50a7be55f1b7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) passage permits and insurance coverage from Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority during the three weeks after the Islamabad MOU was signed and before the latest U.S. attacks, the authority claimed.
* According to the Authority, 79% of requests were approved with insurance issued, 14% remained in progress, and the average permitting process took 50 hours. Tankers accounted for the largest share at 41%, followed by bulk carriers at 27% and container ships at 18%.
* Requests were also nearly evenly divided between vessels exiting the Persian Gulf, 53%, and those entering, 47%. Among outbound requests, 21% were headed to China, 20% to India, and 29% elsewhere in Asia.

* **U.S. announces new sanctions against Iranian businessman:** The U.S. Treasury Department [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/5c837c4f-f522-4899-9774-fc96e20c9a02?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) on Tuesday that it was issuing a new set of sanctions targeting the businesses of Iranian oil magnate Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani.
* Treasury described Shamkhani's "network" as critical to Iran's oil-exporting capacity and said that his businesses now include container shipping and commodities trading concerns, which range from Dubai and Singapore to the Caspian Sea.
* It also said Shamkhani's business was integral to the export of Iranian oil to Russia.
* The sanctions designated financiers, shipping executives, and companies across the UAE, India, Denmark, and Italy. With the action, the Department estimated it had sanctioned more than 200 people or entities with ties to Shamkhani.

* **House to vote on U.S. aid to Israel:** The U.S. House of Representatives is [scheduled](https://substack.com/redirect/7896d99a-4652-44b4-b398-fcf0220410aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) to vote this week on an amendment to a State Department funding bill that would prevent any of its allocated funds from going to Israel.
* The measure, introduced by Republican Rep. **Thomas Massie**(R-Ky.), has been a source of "frenzied internal discussion" among Democratic representatives, according to Axios.
* House Democratic Leader **Hakeem Jeffries** told colleagues he would vote against the bill in a closed-door caucus on Tuesday, calling the measure "overly broad." In a letter to his congressional colleagues explaining his decision, Jeffries said that "American policy in the Middle East must change," but that the U.S. commitment to Israel "must remain ironclad" and any future agreement should preserve Israel's "qualitative military edge."
* Jeffries' decision to [oppose](https://substack.com/redirect/b6184ed4-099b-4bf2-ae73-13c299a5809f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the amendment comes weeks after AIPAC's PAC sent a record $149,300 earmarked contribution to his joint fundraising committee, Sludge reported on Tuesday, the largest earmarked disbursement AIPAC's PAC has ever made, and nearly 30 times the standard $5,000-per-election limit for a multicandidate PAC giving directly to one candidate.
* A May 2026 New York Times/Siena poll found that 74 percent of Democrats opposed providing more economic and military support to Israel, while only 20 percent supported doing so.
* **UAE gains expanded U.S. AI chip access after aiding strikes on Iran** : The United Arab Emirates has [gained](https://substack.com/redirect/ba9c4210-7323-482a-97e5-2a8eb58ea804?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) expanded access to U.S. artificial-intelligence chips after aiding American operations against Iran with airstrikes, missile interceptions, and efforts to keep oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday.

The shift also removes licensing requirements for U.S. firms such as Microsoft and OpenAI that would prevent them from building data centers in the Emirates.
* Emirati officials have lobbied the U.S. on AI access for months, according to WSJ.

* **Man killed during ICE chase in Florida:** A 28-year-old man was struck and [killed](https://substack.com/redirect/47cbcb97-afcc-43ec-86df-683533ceacb6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) by a tractor-trailer on Tuesday morning while fleeing federal immigration agents in St. Augustine, Florida.

* **Gov. Hochul signs first statewide data center moratorium** : New York Gov. **Kathy Hochul** [signed](https://substack.com/redirect/00c8005e-61c9-4408-8c9e-6cbf789000a4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) an executive order Tuesday pausing environmental permits for one year on large data centers using 50 or more megawatts of power, the first statewide ban of its kind in the country.

* **U.S. has refunded $81 billion in illegal tariffs** : The U.S. government has already [refunded](https://substack.com/redirect/443c013b-58a8-407e-a28a-29e7ad7efa40?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) $81 billion in tariffs so far this fiscal year, up from $5 billion during the same period last year, according to budget figures released Monday.

* **Trump meets Iraqi PM al-Zaidi at the White House:** Ali al-Zaidi,**** Iraq's newly elected Prime Minister, [met](https://substack.com/redirect/09b435a4-27f7-42cf-bc44-c2bb2f7b0710?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with President Trump at the White House on Tuesday, with both leaders vowing to deepen their economic ties and to boost Iraqi oil output, according to Al Jazeera.
* At the meeting, Trump called al-Zaidi "a fantastic champion" and promised that both countries would soon "be taking out a lot of oil."
* Both leaders said that the remaining U.S. presence in Iraq would completely withdraw by September 30, the same day on which al-Zaidi has said armed factions within the country will disarm.
* After the meeting, Zaidi also demanded that Iraq be given its "fair share" by the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), citing "$400 billion" in damages from its war against the Islamic State, which Iraq declared over in 2017.

Iran and Ceasefire U.S. resumes naval blockade of Iran and launches new strikes: U.S. Central Command on Tuesday afternoon that American forces had resumed their naval blockade of vessels traveling to and from Iranian ports and coastal areas. An hour earlier, the U.S. launched another round of strikes on Iran, four days after it began its current, ceasefire-shattering round of strikes. Tuesday's U.S. strikes targeted civilian infrastructure in the country, including a wheat warehouse in Hoveyzeh and a mineral-water factory in Dehloran, according to Iranian state media. CENTCOM on Tuesday evening that it had completed a seven-hour wave of strikes on Iran, reporting that it hit dozens of military targets near the Strait of Hormuz and along Iran's southern coast. U.S. strikes hit the city of Bushehr on Wednesday, according to the region's governor, hitting four locations without causing casualties. Another strike on a barracks in the city of Iranshahr reportedly 7 people, mostly soldiers, and wounded 15 others, according to Iran's Tasnim News Agency. U.S. strikes on Wednesday morning, with one strike hitting the Iranian port city of Chabahar. CENTCOM a conclusion to a "90-minute" wave of strikes at 3:00 p.m., Tehran local time. U.S. strikes have more than 30 civilians and wounded 260 others since last week, an Iranian government spokesperson reported. Iran responds, hits U.S. bases in the Gulf: Iran launched several strikes on U.S. bases in the region in response to Washington's continued attacks. One attack set fire to and destroyed a U.S. military logistics and support center at Kuwait's Mina Abdullah port, Iran's military claimed, which supports a vital industrial and refining area south of Kuwait City. Footage of the site showed what appears to be an Iranian drone striking a burning warehouse. The IRGC also claimed it hit several other military targets in Kuwait, including a satellite communications center, a missile- and air-defense radar, a Patriot air-defense complex, and HIMARS launch platforms. Neither the U.S. nor the Kuwaiti governments have any damage, though Kuwait it had intercepted one ballistic missile, five cruise missiles, and 33 hostile drones from Iran on Tuesday evening. Iran also struck and a Kuwaiti naval vessel, wounding four Kuwaiti soldiers, according to the Kuwaiti government, which added that the wounded were in stable condition. Another Iranian strike the U.S. military base at Al-Azraq in Jordan on Tuesday, the IRGC claimed in a statement. Sirens were also on Wednesday morning in Bahrain, which hosts the U.S. Navy's Fleet headquarters and which the IRGC said it struck on Tuesday. Separately, CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper on Tuesday that Iran had attacked seven commercial ships in the past week, in attacks which he claimed killed or wounded nearly a dozen civilian crew members. On Wednesday morning, a cargo ship in the Gulf, though the cause of the incident remains unclear. All 23 of its crew members were rescued, according to Al Jazeera. An unidentified drone also crashed into Iraq's Grand Faw Port, though it reportedly did not interrupt the port's operations. Trump ditches calls for a 20% Hormuz fee: In a Truth Social post on Tuesday morning, U.S. President Donald Trump that he would no longer be pursuing a 20% fee for all ships transiting the Strait of Hormuz and that he would "replace" the non-existent fee with "Trade and Investment Deals that the various Gulf States will be making with the United States." In the post, Trump claimed, despite the ongoing hostilities and Iranian claims to the contrary, that the "Strait is open to ALL Ship traffic except for Iran." Iranian state media reported Wednesday that the Strait has become "impassable" for commercial shipping, with at least two vessels stopped by the IRGC after warning shots were fired over the past 24 hours. Trump threatens strikes on additional Iranian infrastructure: In an interview with Fox News' Trey Yingst on Tuesday, Trump he would strike Iran's power plants and bridges unless Iran's leadership "gets to the table and negotiates" by next week. The threats follow U.S. strikes on a mineral water factory and a wheat warehouse in Iran, reported on Tuesday. He again that the Strait of Hormuz is "open if people want to go through it," though he implied otherwise by speculating on "great alternatives," "including Texas, including Alaska." Trump also Yingst that a ground invasion of Iran's Kharg Island, the vital hub for about 90 percent of the country's oil exports, is "unlikely" for now, though he might reconsider this "if we degrade them far enough and deep enough back." IRGC says there will be "energy for everyone or no one": In to the resumption of the U.S. blockade, the IRGC threatened on Wednesday to prevent all oil exports from the Gulf, saying in a statement, "the export of oil and gas from the region will be either for everyone or for no one." More than 200 vessels ask Iran for permission to transit the Strait, PGSA says: More than 200 non-Iranian vessels passage permits and insurance coverage from Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority during the three weeks after the Islamabad MOU was signed and before the latest U.S. attacks, the authority claimed. According to the Authority, 79% of requests were approved with insurance issued, 14% remained in progress, and the average permitting process took 50 hours. Tankers accounted for the largest share at 41%, followed by bulk carriers at 27% and container ships at 18%. Requests were also nearly evenly divided between vessels exiting the Persian Gulf, 53%, and those entering, 47%. Among outbound requests, 21% were headed to China, 20% to India, and 29% elsewhere in Asia. U.S. announces new sanctions against Iranian businessman: The U.S. Treasury Department on Tuesday that it was issuing a new set of sanctions targeting the businesses of Iranian oil magnate Mohammad Hossein Shamkhani. Treasury described Shamkhani's "network" as critical to Iran's oil-exporting capacity and said that his businesses now include container shipping and commodities trading concerns, which range from Dubai and Singapore to the Caspian Sea. It also said Shamkhani's business was integral to the export of Iranian oil to Russia. The sanctions designated financiers, shipping executives, and companies across the UAE, India, Denmark, and Italy. With the action, the Department estimated it had sanctioned more than 200 people or entities with ties to Shamkhani. In a separate move, Treasury said it sanctioned crypto wallets linked to Iran's Central Bank, freezing more than $130 million in assets. Iran depriving U.S. of alternate route, WSJ reports: Iran's attacks on tankers are off a U.S.-led workaround that kept oil moving through a southern route in the Strait of Hormuz, threatening to reignite one of the worst energy shocks in decades, the Wall Street Journal reported on Tuesday. Two of the three supertankers struck Tuesday were part of a "shuttle run" fleet ferrying crude from Gulf terminals to ports outside the strait, including Fujairah, where it was transferred to ships bound for global markets. The system had been moving about 3.5 million barrels a day, roughly a third of crude exports through Hormuz, according to the Journal. A strike which killed a sailor on Tuesday has reportedly rattled crews, and some captains are now refusing to transit the Strait. The number of ships transiting the Strait on Tuesday slightly on Tuesday, with 21 monitored transits recorded, according to the maritime tracking firm Kpler. The firm noted, however, a "deteriorated" security outlook in the region, with "56 confirmed incidents and 17 seafarer fatalities." Iran executes man for role in winter protests: Iran the execution of Mohammad Amini Dehaghani, "a collaborator with the enemy," on Tuesday, after he was found guilty of throwing a Molotov cocktail outside of a government building in Dehagan in January, ISNA reported. Israel imprisons soldier on charges of spying for Iran: A military court an Israeli soldier to fifteen years in prison on Wednesday for acting as an Iranian spy, the Times of Israel reported without identifying the man, who it claimed exchanged photographs with Iranian agents over Telegram for payment during the 2025 U.S.-Israeli war against Iran. Lebanon Israel destroys buildings and roads in southern Lebanon during "ceasefire": The Israeli military carried out an "explosion operation" on Wednesday in the town of Kounine, in Bint Jbeil district, according to Lebanon's National News Agency. Earlier on Wednesday, Israel buildings in the eastern neighborhood of Khiam, the town of Qantara in the Marjayoun district, and in Beit Yahoun. Israel also fired on people inspecting an orchard near Majdal Zoun, the NNA reported, and bulldozed a road linking Bint Jbeil to the border town of Maroun al-Ras. Palestine Killed and wounded: Over the last 24 hours, 13 Palestinians were killed, one due to wounds sustained in earlier attacks, and 18 were injured in Israeli attacks across Gaza, according to the Palestinian Ministry of Health. The total recorded death toll since October 7, 2023 has risen to 73,246 killed, with 173,727 injured. Since October 11, the first full day of the so-called ceasefire, Israel has killed at least 1,123 Palestinians in Gaza and wounded 3,616, while 800 bodies have been recovered from under the rubble. Israel continues to hit Gaza: An Israeli on Deir Al-Balah early Wednesday morning killed four members of the same family, including a 6-year-old girl, according to WAFA. An Israeli strike on a shelter in Gaza City on Wednesday two Palestinians, according to Al Jazeera Arabic. Israel areas near the Al-Bureij refugee camp and the Shujaiyya neighborhood in Gaza City, continued demolition operations in Qizan Al-Najjar, and dropped bombs in the Bani Suheila roundabout near Khan Younis, with heavy tank fire reported in the city's east. Israeli settlers injure three in the occupied West Bank: Israeli settlers three Palestinians in an attack on the town of Yatta on Wednesday, WAFA reported, with the Palestinians sustaining fractures, cuts, and bruises. Uganda planning deployment to Gaza: Uganda is to deploy troops to Gaza at the request of U.S. President Trump, the state-owned newspaper New Vision reported Monday. According to the paper, Trump asked President Yoweri Museveni, through his "Board of Peace" plan, to contribute forces to the International Stabilization Force in Gaza. Museveni reportedly agreed. An initial deployment of about 500 Ugandan troops is expected to establish a logistics base on the Israeli side of the Kerem Shalom crossing before any move into Gaza, New Vision reported. Israel approves new settlement near Jenin: Israel's security cabinet has approved the establishment of a new settlement in the south of Jenin in the occupied West Bank, according to Israeli media via WAFA. The proposal brings the total number of settlements approved by the government during the past four years to 103, following the approval of 34 new settlements across the occupied West Bank and Jordan Valley in March. Smotrich had previously announced the allocation of 1.3 billion shekels ($434 million) for the settlement project, describing the latest approval as "historic" and saying it was intended to strengthen Israeli control over the occupied West Bank. Drop Site 's Jeremy Scahill debates Rep. Ro Khanna on Israel: On this week's stream, Rep. Ro Khanna describes being detained by Israeli settlers backed by the Israeli army earlier this month--and talks about his meetings with Palestinians in the occupied West Bank. Khanna and Drop Site co-founder Jeremy Scahill debate Palestinian armed resistance, the Iron Dome, and Congress's role. Their full exchange is available . U.S. News By Julian Andreone, with Ryan Grim. Have a tip on Capitol Hill? Email Andreone at. House to vote on U.S. aid to Israel: The U.S. House of Representatives is to vote this week on an amendment to a State Department funding bill that would prevent any of its allocated funds from going to Israel. The measure, introduced by Republican Rep. Thomas Massie(R-Ky.), has been a source of "frenzied internal discussion" among Democratic representatives, according to Axios. House Democratic Leader Hakeem Jeffries told colleagues he would vote against the bill in a closed-door caucus on Tuesday, calling the measure "overly broad." In a letter to his congressional colleagues explaining his decision, Jeffries said that "American policy in the Middle East must change," but that the U.S. commitment to Israel "must remain ironclad" and any future agreement should preserve Israel's "qualitative military edge." Jeffries' decision to the amendment comes weeks after AIPAC's PAC sent a record $149,300 earmarked contribution to his joint fundraising committee, Sludge reported on Tuesday, the largest earmarked disbursement AIPAC's PAC has ever made, and nearly 30 times the standard $5,000-per-election limit for a multicandidate PAC giving directly to one candidate. A May 2026 New York Times/Siena poll found that 74 percent of Democrats opposed providing more economic and military support to Israel, while only 20 percent supported doing so. UAE gains expanded U.S. AI chip access after aiding strikes on Iran : The United Arab Emirates has expanded access to U.S. artificial-intelligence chips after aiding American operations against Iran with airstrikes, missile interceptions, and efforts to keep oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, the Wall Street Journal reported on Wednesday. Under a rule change announced by the Trump administration on Friday, the UAE's main AI company, G42, will be allowed to buy AI chips freely from American companies like Nvidia for at least nine months. The shift also removes licensing requirements for U.S. firms such as Microsoft and OpenAI that would prevent them from building data centers in the Emirates. Emirati officials have lobbied the U.S. on AI access for months, according to WSJ. Officials have also attempted to curry favor with Trump's family, with the country's national security advisor, Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan , investing $500 million in the Trump family's World Liberty Financial venture. Man killed during ICE chase in Florida: A 28-year-old man was struck and by a tractor-trailer on Tuesday morning while fleeing federal immigration agents in St. Augustine, Florida. ICE and Homeland Security Investigations agents approached the man's vehicle at a gas station, causing him and four others to attempt an escape. While crossing State Road 16, he was hit by an oncoming truck and died at the scene. A statement from DHS later reported that the man was a Mexican national. It is the third death connected to an ICE encounter in roughly a week, following two fatal shootings by federal agents, one in Maine and another in Texas. Trump orders ICE to reverse pause on vehicle stops: On Tuesday, Immigration and Customs Enforcement a halt to most vehicle stops nationwide, following two killings by ICE officers in the past week in Houston and Biddeford, Maine. By Tuesday evening Border Czar Tom Homan was insisting the pause would only be temporary, calling it a "short pause." President Donald Trump directed the agency to reverse course in a Wednesday morning Truth Social Post, saying that his administration "CANNOT give up one of I.C.E.'s most important and effective Crime Fighting tools, THE TRAFFIC STOP!" and asserting that such a change would not "happen on my watch." Gov. Hochul signs first statewide data center moratorium : New York Gov. Kathy Hochul an executive order Tuesday pausing environmental permits for one year on large data centers using 50 or more megawatts of power, the first statewide ban of its kind in the country. Hochul said the pause gives the legislature time to craft new laws protecting the electrical grid, environment, and communities, and she also called on lawmakers to repeal sales tax exemptions for data centers. The order won't affect projects that already have permits. The market intelligence company Cleanview lists 25 proposed data centers in New York State, including a controversial project near Ithaca. Senate Democrats block $1.15 trillion defense authorization bill : Senate Democrats a motion to advance the $1.15 trillion National Defense Authorization Act on Tuesday in a 50-46 vote, falling short of the 60 votes needed to advance. Four senators--John Fetterman (D-Pa.), Jim Justice (R-W.Va.), Mitch McConnell(R-Ky.), and Alex Padilla(D-Calif.)--missed the vote. Democratic Party leadership cited the resumed war with Iran, for which President Donald Trump has failed to seek congressional authorization, as the key reason for their opposition. The bill, which cleared committee 18-9 in June, would provide $1.1 trillion to the Defense Department and include a 3.6% pay raise for troops, and also includes a controversial "intelligence sharing" provision, which would effectively integrate the U.S. and Israeli militaries. South Korean company facing U.S. trade probe paid Trump $2 million : Base Group, the lead investor in South Korean aluminum exporter Korea Aluminium, a $2 million payment last year to President Donald Trump's holding company, according to Trump's annual financial disclosure released in late June, the New York Times reported on Tuesday. The disclosure describes the payment as a "nonrefundable development fee" tied to a still-unannounced golf course project, and both Base Group and the Trump family said it is unrelated to Korea Aluminium's dispute with the Commerce Department, which has curbed the company's U.S. exports over findings that it circumvented duties on Chinese aluminum. The payment is part of at least $125 million Trump's company collected last year from foreign sources across more than a dozen countries. New report finds 412 crowd-control weapon "misuse" incidents at U.S. immigration protests: Physicians for Human Rights and the Human Rights Center at the University of California, Berkeley a report on Monday documenting 412 verified incidents of law enforcement misusing crowd-control weapons at anti-immigration protests nationwide between June 2025 and May 2026, resulting in at least 203 confirmed injuries, including blindings, traumatic brain injuries, and fractures. The true number of incidents, the report argues, is likely far greater. More than 90% of the documented incidents occurred in five metro areas--Los Angeles, Chicago, Minneapolis, Newark and Portland--with federal agencies responsible for 64% of cases. Researchers found incident counts rose sharply in each city following the arrival of former Border Patrol commander Gregory Bovino , who led aggressive enforcement surges before retiring in March. Mahmoud Khalil sues federal government over "public-private conspiracy" to suppress anti-Israel speech: Mahmoud Khalil , whose March 2025 arrest while he was a graduate student at Columbia made him the face of Trump's crackdown on pro-Palestinian protest, a lawsuit in Manhattan federal court on Tuesday, saying administration officials and pro-Israel groups conspired to strip him of his constitutional rights, the AP reported. The lawsuit alleges that the federal government worked with pro-Israel organizations and conservative groups to "nearly automatically" target student activists identified by these groups, a "public-private partnership" in violation of the Reconstruction-era Ku Klux Klan Act. The suit names the Heritage Foundation as the alleged architect of the policy, along with pro-Israel groups Canary Mission and Betar. AOC comes out in favor of Israel arms embargo: Rep. Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez Drop Site's Julian Andreone that she now supports a total arms embargo on Israel. Ocasio-Cortez had previously said she would oppose both offensive and defensive weapons aid to Israel. She clarified that her stance now extends to military aid and arms sales, and that she would vote against any bill requiring her to approve the transfer of weapons to Israel. U.S. has refunded $81 billion in illegal tariffs : The U.S. government has already $81 billion in tariffs so far this fiscal year, up from $5 billion during the same period last year, according to budget figures released Monday. The refunds follow a February decision by the Supreme Court, which struck down a sizable portion of the tariffs Trump had ordered and ordered the government to repay companies for the tariffs it had already levied on them. A Treasury Department official said the spike stemmed almost entirely from the ruling, with most refunds issued in May and June. The administration's temporary 10% global tariff expires July 24, though the White House is preparing new duties of 10% to 12.5% on major partners including the U.K., Japan, India, Taiwan, and China. Other International News Ansarallah leader threatens siege of Saudi Arabia: Mohammed Al-Bukhaiti, a member of the political bureau of Yemen's Ansarallah movement, Al Jazeera on Tuesday that the group would lay siege to Saudi Arabia in retaliation for Saudi attacks earlier this week. He attacked Saudi Arabia's "willingness to attack Sanaa Airport to prevent flights from arriving or departing," claiming that this aggression licenses the movement to "strike their airports and to impose" a reciprocal siege on the country. His remarks come after a coalition led by Saudi Arabia struck a runway at Sanaa's airport. The strikes coincided with the arrival of a flight carrying an Ansarallah delegation returning from the deceased Ayatollah Khomeini's funeral. That delegation included Al-Bukhaiti. Ansarallah responded by launching strikes at Saudi Arabia's Abha International Airport. No casualties were reported in either incident. Amir-Saeid Iravani, Iran's permanent representative to the UN, on the attacks Wednesday, saying that claims that Ansarallah is acting on behalf of Iran were "completely baseless," and that the movement makes "its decisions independently and in accordance with what they consider to be the interests of the Yemeni people." Cuba 's power grid collapses for third time this month: Cuba's national power grid again on Tuesday, plunging nearly 10 million people into darkness. It is the country's third nationwide blackout in eight days and the fifth since the Trump administration imposed its oil blockade in late January. The U.S. blockade has cut off Cuba's supplies of foreign fuel, crippling its aging power plants. Public transportation has largely halted, tens of thousands of surgeries have been canceled, and routine outages now leave some communities without electricity for more than 20 hours a day. Mexico files criminal complaints over ICE deaths: Mexico has begun criminal complaints with state prosecutors in the U.S. in response to the deaths of its citizens in ICE detention and during immigration enforcement operations, according to a statement from the country's foreign ministry on Tuesday, after Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum said on Friday that her government could not "turn a blind eye to the Mexicans who have died." At least 14 Mexican nationals have died in ICE custody, and several others, including Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, have died during arrests. The government has also cease-and-desist letters to ICE detention centers where its nationals have died, Reuters reported. The foreign ministry also contacted the United Nations High Commissioner for Human Rights, asking the office of the Commissioner to gather additional information about the deaths of Mexican nationals in the U.S. Two Nepali ministers jailed over immigration scam: A Nepali court two former government ministers to jail on Tuesday, convicting them of forging documents to allow Nepali nationals to be resettled in the U.S. as Bhutanese refugees, Reuters reported. Top Bahadur Rayamajhi, a former deputy prime minister and energy minister, was sentenced to four years for fraud and "involvement in organized crime," and Bal Krishna Khand, the country's former home minister, was sentenced two years for acting as Rayamajhi's accomplice. Over 100,000 ethnic Nepalis have fled from Bhutan since the 1990s after the Bhutanese government stripped thousands of ethnic Nepalis of their citizenship, and the majority of these refugees have been resettled in third countries, including the U.S. and Canada. Fourteen others, including at least one who worked in Khand's Home Ministry, were sentenced to up to 4 years in jail in connection with the scam. Fifty migrants missing after boat capsizes in the Mediterranean: At least 50 migrants were feared at sea after their boat capsized off the eastern coast of Libya on Tuesday, security sources told Reuters, noting that 10 migrants on the ship had survived. The majority of the immigrants hail from countries in sub-Saharan Africa. On Monday, rescue teams off the coast of Tobruk, rescued 24 migrants and recovered the bodies of four others. A similar incident near the city in June killed 26 people. Nine dead from clashes in Pakistan 's Kashmir: Clashes between Pakistani security forces and supporters of the Joint Action Committee, a proscribed protest group, killed seven protesters and two police officers Tuesday in Pakistan-administered Kashmir, Reuters . The violence comes a day before a march protesting regional elections planned for later this month. The event is planned in Rawalakot, a district capital in Pakistan's Azad Kashmir. Locals are protesting seats reserved for Kashmiri refugees who live in other parts of Pakistan, an arrangement they claim dilutes their representation in the regional assembly. At least 30 people have died in protest-related violence in Pakistani Kashmir since June. RSF submits response to truce proposal: Sudan's Rapid Support Forces paramilitary group its response on Tuesday to a series of peace proposals introduced by U.S. Senior Advisor for Arab and African Affairs Massad Boulos, accepting a political settlement under its outlined conditions but refusing to withdraw from territories it has captured, according to Sudan Tribune. Boulos' plan, introduced in June, calls for a 90-day humanitarian truce, a transitional political process, a comprehensive ceasefire, and the start of the country's reconstruction. The RSF's response includes a set of conditions related to security arrangements, the reconstitution of state institutions, the administration of justice during a transitional period, and details concerning the path to a transitional government. Sudan's Army submitted its response on July 12 and has rejected a "gradual settlement" akin to what the RSF has introduced in its counterproposal. Russia to divert exports away from Azov: Russia's Ministry of Agriculture on Tuesday that it was preparing to use "alternative shipping routes" and to redirect cargo "to other modes of transport" after Ukraine attacked several Russian vessels in the Sea of Azov overnight, AFP reported. A Ukrainian military commander claimed Tuesday's attacks hit 11 Russian vessels, including five tankers, five dry cargo vessels and a tugboat, bringing the total number of vessels hit in the past nine days to 116. Ukraine also launched strikes on Russia's energy infrastructure, hitting refineries in the Caucasian province of Krasnodar and the southern province of Bashkortostan. Russia claimed it hit Kyiv for the second consecutive day and damaged port infrastructure in Odesa, where the Ukrainian navy reported damage to a civilian vessel. Russia says foreign troops in postwar Ukraine would be military targets: At a press conference Russian officials that any multinational force deployed to Ukraine after a peace agreement would be treated as an unacceptable foreign intervention and a legitimate target for Russian forces. The warning came after Western members of the "coalition of the willing" reaffirmed plans to send a Multinational Force for Ukraine following a ceasefire and announced exercises intended to demonstrate its readiness. "This would amount, de facto, to foreign intervention and an escalation of threats to Russia's security," Russian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Maria Zakharova said. "We would regard such units as legitimate military targets." Trump meets Iraqi PM al-Zaidi at the White House: Ali al-Zaidi,** Iraq's newly elected Prime Minister, with President Trump at the White House on Tuesday, with both leaders vowing to deepen their economic ties and to boost Iraqi oil output, according to Al Jazeera. At the meeting, Trump called al-Zaidi "a fantastic champion" and promised that both countries would soon "be taking out a lot of oil." Both leaders said that the remaining U.S. presence in Iraq would completely withdraw by September 30, the same day on which al-Zaidi has said armed factions within the country will disarm. After the meeting, Zaidi also demanded that Iraq be given its "fair share" by the Organization of the Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC), citing "$400 billion" in damages from its war against the Islamic State, which Iraq declared over in 2017. ---
## **News from the Campaign Trail**
|
---

**One year later...**
After Lloyd Smucker led the passage of the massive legislative package known as the “One Big Beautiful Bill” in July 2025, PA-11 residents are feeling the impact. In this district alone, an estimated 3,500 people have lost SNAP benefits and nearly 14,000 have lost Medicaid coverage. Combined with the escalating costs of food, housing, and gasoline, many of our neighbors are struggling to make ends meet, put food on the table, and pray they don’t get sick. I’ve had worried residents tell me they are splitting their pills or taking them every other day instead of daily to stretch their supply. Food pantries across the district report a surge in demand as families attempt to provide meals for their children.
This legislation delivered $5 trillion dollars in tax cuts to billionaires while the average working family can expect about $800 in tax relief. Who is Lloyd Smucker really working for?
And the worst is still ahead. In January 2027, additional Republican-backed cuts and restrictions to health and nutrition benefits are set to take effect—delayed to avoid harming Republicans in the midterm elections.
As a nurse, I know how vital affordable healthcare and healthy food are. I will fight to reverse budget cuts that hurt Pennsylvanians and restore essential programs that protect the health and safety of all Americans.
Nancy

### **Week in Review:**
**Marking the 8th Town Hall in Hellam**
Thank you to everyone who joined us for the Hellam Township Town Hall on July 9.Accountability is more than a campaign promise—it is a responsibility. Anyone asking for the privilege of representing a community should be willing to stand before it. Since February, Nancy has held eight town halls across Lancaster and York Counties and will continue holding them in Congress. The people of PA-11 deserve a representative who listens, answers tough questions, and shows up when it matters.
Thank you for your time, thoughtful questions, and commitment to being part of the conversation. Nancy will keep showing up because that is what public service requires.
**Celebrating York County on Saturday**
On Saturday, July 11, Nancy visited the southernmost parts of York County to join local community celebrations. First, she met future constituents at the Snack Town Festival in Hanover; later that afternoon, she traveled to Delta to take part in the Delta-Cardiff Volunteer Fire Company’s Fireman’s Parade.

clean_body: | | | | | News from the Campaign Trail | One year later... After Lloyd Smucker led the passage of the massive legislative package known as the “One Big Beautiful Bill” in July 2025, PA-11 residents are feeling the impact. In this district alone, an estimated 3,500 people have lost SNAP benefits and nearly 14,000 have lost Medicaid coverage. Combined with the escalating costs of food, housing, and gasoline, many of our neighbors are struggling to make ends meet, put food on the table, and pray they don’t get sick. I’ve had worried residents tell me they are splitting their pills or taking them every other day instead of daily to stretch their supply. Food pantries across the district report a surge in demand as families attempt to provide meals for their children. This legislation delivered $5 trillion dollars in tax cuts to billionaires while the average working family can expect about $800 in tax relief. Who is Lloyd Smucker really working for? And the worst is still ahead. In January 2027, additional Republican-backed cuts and restrictions to health and nutrition benefits are set to take effect—delayed to avoid harming Republicans in the midterm elections. As a nurse, I know how vital affordable healthcare and healthy food are. I will fight to reverse budget cuts that hurt Pennsylvanians and restore essential programs that protect the health and safety of all Americans. Nancy | Enjoying These Campaign Updates? clean_body: | | | Michigan's congressional races are the next major test for our movement, Peter. Working Families champions have won 16 competitive congressional primaries this cycle. Now the wealthiest interests in the country are fighting back. AIPAC, Big Tech companies racing to build AI data centers, crypto billionaires, and other wealthy interests are pouring millions into Michigan because they know every Working Families champion we elect threatens business as usual in Washington. That's why they're trying to stop Abdul El-Sayed, Will Lawrence, and Donavan McKinney before they ever get there. This is a virtual event you can join from anywhere. All you need is a laptop and headphones. Never phonebanked before? No worries — we'll start with a training, and experienced volunteers will be there every step of the way. Donavan has spent his career fighting for the people of Detroit — from organizing alongside healthcare workers to delivering real results in the Michigan legislature. He's seen what it means when families work hard but still struggle to afford groceries, pay the rent, or keep up with rising costs. That's whyhe's running for Congress: to make sure working people finally have someone in Washington who's fighting for them. It’s also why he's earned the support of House progressives like Bernie Sanders and Rashida Tlaib. And it’s exactlywhy the same powerful interests driving up costs for Detroit families — from crypto PACs to utility companies — are bankrolling his opponent instead. If Donavan wins, he'll join a growing bloc of Working Families champions in Congress who know exactly who sent them to Washington, and who they'll be accountable to:the workers, parents, caregivers, and families counting on them to build an economy that works for everyone, not just the wealthy few. That means one more vote for the people who keep this country running — teachers, nurses, warehouse workers, bus drivers, grocery clerks, and the other millions of people who work hard every day and deserve a government that works just as hard for them. One more vote against the corporations squeezing families on every bill, every paycheck, and every prescription. One more vote to build an economy where working people can finally get ahead instead of just trying to survive. You don't have to live in Michigan to have a stake in who represents Michigan in Congress, Peter. The corporate money flooding this race is national. But our movement is too. | | **🫵 WAIT! 🫵**
**❌ STOP WHAT YOU’RE DOING ❌**

**But Democrats are SOUNDING THE ALARM, and they need you to defend our democracy.**

[We’re sending an emergency letter demanding the Postal Service do the right thing. They need to know we’re not backing down! Add your name before our midnight deadline »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/117680?t=7&akid=26357%2E878179%2EQQe0Nj) | [SIGN THE LETTER ASAP: DEMAND USPS PROTECT MAIL-IN VOTING »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/117680?t=8&akid=26357%2E878179%2EQQe0Nj)

TO: U.S. Postal Service
FROM: A furious Democrat
Subject: Please don’t cave to Trump.

Dear USPS,

**I am writing today to DEMAND that you stand up to Donald Trump and PROTECT vote-by-mail.**

Vote-by-mail has expanded voting access to millions of Americans in rural areas, serving overseas, and in marginalized communities.

Limiting access to states who do Trump’s bidding is UNDEMOCRATIC and straight up AUTHORITARIAN!

The Postal Service is a vital institution that has done so much good for our country — **so please don’t sacrifice everything you stand for now.**

[I’m signing this letter today to DEMAND you stand up to Trump and this disgusting attack on voting rights. # [Iran Sent Message to JD Vance Warning that Kushner and Witkoff Were "Abusing" Their Inside Access to Negotiations](https://substack.com/app-link/post?publication_id=2510348&post_id=207177553&utm_source=post-email-title&utm_campaign=email-post-title&isFreemail=true&r=1hvr60&token=eyJ1c2VyX2lkIjo5MDUwMTE5MiwicG9zdF9pZCI6MjA3MTc3NTUzLCJpYXQiOjE3ODQxMzQ1ODgsImV4cCI6MTc4NjcyNjU4OCwiaXNzIjoicHViLTI1MTAzNDgiLCJzdWIiOiJwb3N0LXJlYWN0aW9uIn0.a6cK6obGF4wPksi3dbmaDhJ6VXzwZbddA1v35UX9b_A)

[Support Drop Site Today](https://substack.com/redirect/661e559e-5dfa-4f60-93aa-8be0eb466caf?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7be8110b-36cb-4b94-b362-965c03d54801?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Vice President JD Vance before a meeting between the United States, Iran, Pakistan and Qatar in Lake Lucerne, Switzerland, on June 21, 2026. Photo by Fabrice Coffrini / POOL / AFP via Getty Images.
During the U.S.-Iran talks in Lake Lucerne, Switzerland in late June, Iranian negotiators sent a private message to Vice President JD Vance through an intermediary. The Iranians warned Vance that the continued presence of President Donald Trump's Special Envoy Steve Witkoff and son-in-law Jared Kushner would undermine the chance of turning the June 17 framework into an enduring deal, a senior Iranian official told Drop Site.
The Iranian official spoke to Drop Site on the condition of anonymity because he is not authorized to speak publicly. In the message, according to the official, Iran conveyed to Vance that the pair were more interested in exploiting insider knowledge of the negotiations to profit in financial markets than they were in reaching a deal. Iranian negotiators also expressed concern about repeated leaks from Kushner to Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. (A U.S. official told [Axios](https://substack.com/redirect/0e2210be-a9ef-4232-b241-5e97f7673700?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that since the negotiations began, Witkoff and Kushner "talk almost every day to Netanyahu" and the head of Mossad.)
In the weeks leading up to the signing of the memorandum of understanding, the official said, Iran presented written documentation to mediators of what it characterized as evidence that "individuals close to President Trump" were abusing the Iran war and diplomatic developments to manipulate financial markets. "Even before the Islamabad talks kicked off [in April], we had already sent multiple messages to Trump through the Pakistanis, warning them about [Witkoff's] overall destructive role in the previous negotiation," the Iranian official said.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuZHJvcHNpdGVuZXdzLmNvbS9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.JMd6R9Y8-NLD3fLYao6opKsTFAwn3Reeqx86yeqOndQ?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=207177553)
The outreach to Vance came after these**** previous efforts to raise Tehran's concerns about Witkoff and Kushner with the White House, the official said--given that**** messages passed to mediators are delivered broadly to the full U.S. team including Kushner, who is a private citizen with no official government role.
"We transmitted data and assessments through an exclusive channel to Mr. Vance," said the senior Iranian official, who has direct knowledge of the effort. Iranian negotiators, he said, communicated to Vance that they believed Witkoff and Kushner were "abusing" the diplomatic process, "effectively disrupting the overall negotiating atmosphere."
Drop Site was not able to independently confirm the intermediary actually delivered the message, though the Iranian official said Tehran was confident Vance had received it. The official declined to offer specifics. In response to a request for comment sent to the vice president's office, a U.S. official denied Iran's claims. "A message of this nature was never conveyed to the Vice President or his team," the official told Drop Site. "Additionally, any insinuation that the other members of the president's trusted negotiating team are operating under motives other than serving the president and delivering on his mission is false."
Kushner and Witkoff did not respond to requests for comment, but a White House spokesperson denied Iran's claims and denounced Drop Site. "No such message was ever transmitted to the United States. It's sad that Drop Site News 'reporters' are so filled with hate for America and devoid of respect for themselves that they have become full-throated propagandists for the Iranian regime," said White House spokesperson Anna Kelly.
A source close to Vance told Drop Site the Iranians had made no secret of their objections to the presence of Witkoff and Kushner in the negotiations.
Since the Iran war began, many financial analysts have described a [pattern](https://substack.com/redirect/3f68ddd7-1651-42e1-a5e5-9608b0c36a80?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) where speculative bets are placed or unusually large positions are taken in [key markets](https://substack.com/redirect/7290496c-3057-4ef1-8efe-2852b8a5d6df?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) related to the conflict and diplomatic events, including consistent announcements from Trump made just prior to the Monday openings of U.S. trading. This has led to widespread [public speculation](https://substack.com/redirect/315ccc0a-54a8-414d-83a6-645e641e9250?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that people with access to inside information are manipulating markets in oil futures, energy stocks, and prediction markets.
In June, Iran calculated profits from such alleged manipulation had reached $9 billion and formally requested, in writing, that Iran should share in the proceeds. "We have conveyed through intermediaries that $4.5 billion of this sum should also be allocated to the Iranian side," the Iranian official said. "The exchanged texts will ultimately become part of the historical record."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/a0c26696-29e3-4ba0-b07b-dd871a2081f7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Trump's son-in-law Jared Kushner and US President's special envoy Steve Witkoff in Lake Lucerne, Switzerland. Photo by URS FLUEELER / POOL / AFP via Getty Images.
Iran met for indirect diplomatic talks on February 6 in Oman and February 26 in Switzerland before the war began on February 28. "During our negotiation rounds in Oman, it had become completely clear to us that this person [Witkoff] had zero connection to diplomacy or actually advancing the talks," the official added, saying that Witkoff had entirely misrepresented Iran's positions on a range of issues, including what terms it was willing to offer the U.S. on the fate of its highly enriched uranium. Witkoff's "mistaken impressions from the negotiations got passed on to Trump," he charged.
The official cautioned that Iran was not naive in believing that Vance would subvert Trump's positions, but assessed that the vice president brings a more sober, professional, and realistic perspective to the negotiations. "Sending this exact message directly to Vance was done with the full approval of our negotiating team," he said. He declined to "confirm or deny anything about other messages being exchanged" between Vance and Iranian officials.
A source close to Vance, however, said the vice president is broadly looking for partners on the Iranian side. "JD is doing the job of what you're supposed to do with diplomacy, which is find people within the other side who are more willing to dialogue, and that's been a real key thing," the U.S. source told Drop Site. "And to be honest, it's diplomacy 101, when you go in and you assess the team, you always try to get as many people on the other team as possible, like you don't want it to be one on one. You want it to be like 12 on 12."
The Iranians also want to see an expansion of the size of the negotiating delegations, particularly technical experts and Iran country experts from the U.S. "We have also informed [Vance] that an expansion of our negotiating team would provide a suitable opportunity for him to adjust the composition of his own delegation," said the senior Iran official.
"That being said, our assessment is that he is cautiously adding select members of his... team with expertise on the Middle East and Iran file, while facing significant constraints in making rapid changes to his team."
The Iranian official dismissed the suggestion Vance would be able to succeed in cultivating an Iranian source on the negotiating team. "The Iranian side has a small, stable team at the high levels, and the scope of their decisions is very clearly defined," the Iranian official said.
The Iranian official said that during the diplomatic talks in Oman and Switzerland before the war, Witkoff and Kushner showed up with no subject area or nuclear experts and appeared oblivious to the technical aspects of negotiating the nuclear issue. During these talks, he said, Iranian negotiators presented an outline of their existing stockpile of enriched uranium and assessed that their "unbelievable level of flexibility" formed the basis for what Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi said on February 25 could be a "historic opportunity to strike an unprecedented agreement."
Witkoff subsequently portrayed Iran's disclosure of its highly enriched uranium stockpile as a threat to build multiple nuclear weapons. "The Iranian negotiators said to us, directly, with, you know, no shame, that they controlled 460 kilograms of 60%, and they're aware that that could make 11 nuclear bombs, and that was the beginning of their negotiating stance," Witkoff said on Fox News on March 3, while defending the decision to attack Iran in the middle of negotiations.
While the Western press routinely characterize the Iranian negotiating team as in disarray, it has been the American side that has been hardest to read, as Trump has periodically disrupted talks with explicit death threats against negotiators, or promised widespread destruction of civilian infrastructure in Iran, after having agreed in the memorandum of understanding to stop leveling such threats.
Just as the talks between Iran and Vance began in Lucerne, Trump appeared to threaten the lives of Iran's negotiators, telling FOX News that if Iran closed the Strait of Hormuz again, "You won't have a country. You won't even make it back to your f***ing country." In response, Iran's delegation staged a walkout of the talks.
"Trump's [statements] during Vance's negotiations with the Iranian delegation in Pakistan and Switzerland [were] clearly intended to undermine Vance's position in the talks," said the Iranian official. "In practice, it ended up weakening his standing with the mediators as well."
The Iranians decided to pursue a direct channel to Vance after the MOU was signed, in part persuaded by mediators that the vice president had a genuine interest in reaching a lasting agreement and that he represented the long-term interests of the U.S. government. Trump, mediators told Iran, appeared driven primarily by his day-to-day feelings as to how the war or the ceasefire reflected on his image. Iran is aware of the political reality that Vance is jockeying for the Republican nomination to succeed Trump, giving him more of an incentive to reach a durable resolution.
"The mediators firmly maintain that President Trump's personal preferences and his disruptive interventions in the peace process are actions that undermine the peace efforts," said the Iranian official. "The mediators are making a distinction between Vance's representation and Trump's own positions. They're saying that Trump personally has an interest in keeping the image of the war going, while the U.S. establishment, represented by Vance, wants to bring the war to a conclusion."
Robert Malley, a former Middle East official under both President Barack Obama and Joe Biden who was also a top U.S. negotiator of the 2015 Iran nuclear deal, said it is strategically sound for the Iranians to work to establish direct communication with Vance, but such a channel can only mean so much.
"Vance may be more authoritative than Kushner and Witkoff, but that hardly makes him authoritative," Malley told Drop Site. "If today's President Trump cannot speak for tomorrow's, then how could JD Vance?"
Still, he said, there's little harm in trying. "It makes perfect sense for the Iranians to try to establish a separate channel to Vice President Vance: He is the most senior U.S. official ever to have met with representatives of the Islamic Republic; he is known to have been skeptical of the war; a diplomatic breakthrough with Tehran would strengthen his political standing; and he is far more dependable than any of the available alternatives--namely, Kushner and Witkoff," he said. "However hard the vice president may try to persuade the Iranians that his word matters more than the president's latest outburst, they would probably be wiser to bet on the outburst rather than the word."
The future of any deal between Iran and the U.S. is very much in doubt. Trump formally informed Congress on July 10 that the U.S. is officially engaged in combat operations against Iran and he publicly declared the ceasefire dead. He has also suggested that diplomatic talks will continue. [On Tuesday, ](https://substack.com/redirect/4d51e840-1293-4da2-8878-58d59fec7ebb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)Trump said that after new U.S. attacks there would not be "anybody left" in Iran.
From Iran's perspective, it's a familiar pattern of the U.S. constructing a mirage of negotiations between attacks. "Under the current circumstances, the U.S. side needs to reassess its understanding of the situation on the ground. They seem determined to test their chances of using force in relation to the Strait of Hormuz," said the Iranian official. "Our view is that once they fail again over the Strait of Hormuz, they'll almost certainly come back to the negotiating table. But by then, the negotiations definitely won't be as straightforward for them as they once were."

I want to tell you a quick story. When I was a young boy, my grandmother passed away. I still went to school that morning, bearing the weight of the news, and I thought nobody would know or care much about what had happened.
But when I got to my classroom, my third-grade teacher, Mrs. Batchelor, greeted me with a hug at the door. She already knew about my grandmother and told me how sorry she was. That small gesture meant the world to me.
I still think about that day all these years later. Teachers are so much more than educators. They're the heart of every community - there for our children during good days and bad - and they deserve to be treated as such.
I attended public schools all the way from first grade through college and law school. And I also saw how hard my mother worked as a public school teacher. She spent early mornings and late nights -- and weekends -- preparing for class and finding new ways to help her students learn.
Public schools are the glue that hold our communities together. It's where we gather for football games, concerts, pancake suppers, quiz bowls and more. Where parents can see their children thrive in academics, art, music, theater and athletics. Public schools define our communities.
When I was Governor, we invested more than $1 billion in early care and learning and expanded Pre-K access. These grants helped us increase teacher pay and allowed schools to better address classroom needs.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/db301e95-a3ed-46f1-8170-97f62469bd60?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/73162c22-2625-4426-9c14-3783913b5227?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
We also expanded initiatives like the Teaching Fellows program to three additional schools, including two historically Black colleges and universities.
Public schools are focused on educating students today so that they can achieve success tomorrow. That's why we created innovative workforce programs like the Longleaf Commitment Grants which invested in high school seniors from low- and middle-income families and helped them afford college tuition. We also created Workforce Resilience Grants to connect eligible community college students with workforce pathways that resulted in a state or industry recognized credential.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/c93f3184-8b02-4c46-9008-79c920da9c26?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Every investment we made in our teachers, classrooms and students was grounded in my belief that children deserve educational tools and opportunities to build their future. That's what Mrs. Batchelor understood when she opened her arms to a grieving child and it's what my mother understood every time she dedicated nights and weekends to her students.
I fought for our students and teachers in the Governor's office, and I promise to fight for them in the U.S. Senate.

name: Internal Team
subject: 20 Days to Go — Get Involved This Week!
body:
Hi all,

My name is Sara, and I recently jumped into the volunteer coordinator role
for Kevin's campaign. We are in the final stretch- 20 days to the primary!
Door knocking and phone banking are the most impactful things we can do
right now, and every conversation counts.

Kevin refuses corporate PAC money, fights for Medicare for All, and
actually shows up for working people in Eastern Washington. We have a
chance to send a true progressive to Congress who works for us. Let's make
it happen!

Feel free to reply, text, Slack, or call me anytime. I will be sending
weekly emails to keep everyone in the loop. If you would like to be removed
from this list, just let me know.

If anyone wants to host a canvassing party and invite friends, I am happy
to help coordinate. Let's make democracy fun! I am also hosting a house
party in the Perry area to celebrate volunteers and help get out the vote.
Would love to see you there!

*Get Out The Vote*

Talk to everyone you know, make sure they are registered, and if they are
not, help them get there. You can register at VoteWA
<https://voter.votewa.gov/portal2023/login.aspx> right up to election day.
We especially need to reach people who have not historically voted. Those
are the voices that can change this race. Ask them, help them, bring them
in!

*Upcoming Events*

-

Tonight: First phone banking session, open doors from 3pm to 7pm. Come
learn how to phone bank! Instructions are also listed on Slack if you want
to do it on your own time. Join via Zoom
<http://salesforce.zoom.us/j/84546637696?pwd=tvZu6DFIZ4jixopuetKtSGIr2fQlHn>
-

This week: Most door knocking is out of the Spokane area in Colville and
Walla Walla. Let me know if you are interested, and I will share times and
locations!
-

Saturday, July 18th: South Hill canvassing before the ice cream social &
tabling at candidate meet & greet ice cream social. Meet at Comstock Park,
and door knock 10am to 1pm. Ice Cream Social is 12-3pm. Even if you can
only show up for 30 minutes, that is incredible!
-

Sunday, July 19th: Kendall Yards and West Central canvassing 11am to
4pm, meeting at Olmsted Park by Hello Sugar. Come when you can, leave when
you want to!
-

Monday, July 20th: Volunteer Barbecue 4pm-8pm in Perry area: Come write
postcards, door-knock, connect, and eat good food! RSVP below.

Please do not hesitate to reach out with any questions. We are so grateful
to have you with us and cannot wait to see what we accomplish together.
Let's go get this thing done!

RSVP for Volunteer Party <http://partiful.com/e/iPqSa2xxDEgD7r7GoNyg>

Join Our Slack
<http://join.slack.com/t/kevinforcongressgroup/shared_invite/zt-41awqi9a8-YUXby_uhQWTV5PXhAHrHng>

Sign Up to Volunteer! <http://forms.gle/aRFnm6FwKJMnD2R77>

Request a Yard Sign <http://forms.gle/DmDsJ25nVbGRSUiq5>
Thank you all,
*Sara Lambdin*
Volunteer Coordinator | 509-481-7471
*Kevin Fagan for Congress — WA-5*
KevinFaganForCongress <http://KevinFaganForCongress.com> |
@kevinfaganforcongress <https://www.instagram.com/kevinfaganforcongress/>
*Building the future we deserve in the Inland Northwest · *
*Primary: August 4, 2026*

We have a chance to send a true progressive to Congress who works for us. Let's make it happen! Feel free to reply, text, Slack, or call me anytime. I will be sending weekly emails to keep everyone in the loop. If you would like to be removed from this list, just let me know. If anyone wants to host a canvassing party and invite friends, I am happy to help coordinate. Let's make democracy fun! I am also hosting a house party in the Perry area to celebrate volunteers and help get out the vote. Would love to see you there! Get Out The Vote Talk to everyone you know, make sure they are registered, and if they are not, help them get there. You can register at VoteWA <> right up to election day. We especially need to reach people who have not historically voted. Those are the voices that can change this race. Ask them, help them, bring them in! Upcoming Events - Tonight: First phone banking session, open doors from 3pm to 7pm. Come learn how to phone bank! Instructions are also listed on Slack if you want to do it on your own time. Join via Zoom <> - This week: Most door knocking is out of the Spokane area in Colville and Walla Walla. Let me know if you are interested, and I will share times and locations! - Saturday, July 18th: South Hill canvassing before the ice cream social & tabling at candidate meet & greet ice cream social. Meet at Comstock Park, and door knock 10am to 1pm. Ice Cream Social is 12-3pm. Even if you can only show up for 30 minutes, that is incredible! - Sunday, July 19th: Kendall Yards and West Central canvassing 11am to 4pm, meeting at Olmsted Park by Hello Sugar. Come when you can, leave when you want to! - Monday, July 20th: Volunteer Barbecue 4pm-8pm in Perry area: Come write postcards, door-knock, connect, and eat good food! RSVP below. Please do not hesitate to reach out with any questions. We are so grateful to have you with us and cannot wait to see what we accomplish together. Let's go get this thing done! RSVP for Volunteer Party <> Join Our Slack <> Sign Up to Volunteer! <> Request a Yard Sign <> Thank you all, Sara Lambdin Volunteer Coordinator | 509-481-7471 Kevin Fagan for Congress — WA-5 KevinFaganForCongress <> | @kevinfaganforcongress <> Building the future we deserve in the Inland Northwest · Primary: August 4, 2026

Peter, one of our wonderful volunteers surprised me with this cake recently, and it made my day.
I often remind people that in fact “Courage is contagious.” I believe it with everything I have — especially right now.
Over the past year and a half, ICE agents have flooded our communities and terrorized our neighbors. Republicans have stripped millions of people of their healthcare to hand tax cuts to the wealthy. Reproductive rights — foundational rights that women held for fifty years — have been ripped away, and the attempts to control women’s bodies keep coming. Our democracy itself is under pressure in ways that would have been unthinkable just a few years ago.
It would be easy to look at all of that and feel overwhelmed — to tell yourself there’s nothing you can do. You’re not alone in feeling that way.
But we cannot look away. This moment demands our engagement. It asks us to have the courage to do what’s right, no matter how difficult.
And luckily, we’ve seen here in Minnesota that when one person stands up, something shifts. When one person speaks out, marches, shows up, and refuses to back down, it gives someone else permission to do the same. And then another. And another.
I’m talking about courage , passed from one person to the next.
That's how movements are built, and that's how we will win in November.
I'm asking you to be courageous right now, in whatever way you can. Show up, speak out, chip in. And trust that your courage matters, not just for what it accomplishes, but for who it inspires.
Will you join me? If you’re in a position to support this work, you can chip in to my re-election campaign using this secure link here: https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/morrison-em-26]

The earthquakes in Venezuela dominated the news for a matter of days. The collapsed buildings, the death toll, the rescue teams pulling survivors from the rubble, **the world watched, then largely moved on.** But for the children left behind, the danger didn't end when the ground stopped shaking. **In some ways, it was only the beginning.** Displacement does something traffickers understand better than almost anyone. It breaks the systems that normally protect a child -- records, schools, familiar faces, parents who never let go of their hand. In that broken space, a stranger offering "help," a ride, a promise of safety somewhere else, can be all it takes for a child to disappear.

And I've learned that disasters like the one in Venezuela don't create new evil, they simply hand existing evil an opening it has used again and again. If this is the first time you're hearing from me, my name is Eduardo Verastegui, and I produced the film Sound of Freedom. The film Sound of Freedom was truly a movie that launched a movement. That movement is now. Our mission at the **Sound of Freedom Foundation** is to **stop the sale of God's children.** We do that through five pillars:
---
* **Prevention**
* **Intervention**
* **Education**
* **Information**
* **Influence**

---
We are working urgently, with trusted partners on the ground, to:
---
* Find children who have already fallen into trafficking, including exploitation happening online in the chaos of the disaster.
* Support rescue operations that bring a child out of danger and into safety.
* Provide a safe bed the moment a child is free.
* Fund reunification when a family can be found and verified.
* Walk alongside a child through long-term care when there is nowhere safe to send them yet.
