body:
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]
The New York Times is reporting that ICE arrested 10,000 people in just five days — a massive increase in immigration arrests that have been intentionally conducted under the radar.
https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25 [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=25]
Let’s be clear about what these numbers actually mean: These are not and never were targeted immigration enforcement to go after “violent criminals” as this administration loves to claim. These are unfocused and chaotic mass arrests to fulfill arbitrary quotas set by DHS.
They’re going after our neighbors, our community members, and people who have built their lives here.
Right now, more than 63,000 people are sitting in ICE detention facilities, including in facilities where people have died. In less than two weeks, ICE agents shot and killed two people: Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, who was on his way to his construction job in Houston, Texas, and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero, a 26-year-old man in Biddeford, Maine. This year alone, 21 people have died while in ICE custody (that we know of).
And earlier this year, Donald Trump signed into law a bill giving ICE an additional $70 billion — without ANY guardrails on how it can be used. This money does nothing to lower the cost of your groceries, your health care, or your housing. It won’t fund your kids’ schools or keep your neighbor from going hungry.
Instead, it went to recruit more masked ICE agents to terrorize our communities, detain record numbers of vulnerable people, including children, and hold them in horrifically inhumane conditions. This money continues to fund a rogue agency that kills Americans in the street in broad daylight, defies federal judges, and inflicts trauma on young children and their families.
It’s American taxpayers who are footing the bill for this, not Donald Trump — and it’s not OK.
I will not stop fighting to end mass detention, dismantle and overhaul ICE, and shut down the horrific family detention centers that are profiting from these human rights abuses.
To do that, we need to take back the House and shut down the corrupt, chaotic, and cruel MAGA majority that’s enabling this brutal administration.
Will you join my efforts to flip the House? Your donations go directly to our work on the ground, making sure I’m re-elected, supporting frontline Democratic colleagues in tough races, and boosting Democratic challengers working to flip red seats. DONATE NOW [https://secure.actblue.com/donate/sjj-em?amount=50]
For the last year and a half, Republicans have been doing Donald Trump’s bidding. But in November, we’re going to make them answer for it.
-Sara

Peter,
The White House announced that Donald Trump will address the nation on Thursday night, and news sources are confirming that Trump will "share declassified intelligence" that "reveals a foreign nation's plans to interfere in the 2020 presidential election."
But that's not all: sources claiming to be close to the White House have said that Trump also intends to declare that Georgia's two Democratic US Senators, Raphael Warnock and Jon Ossoff, are "illegitimate."

name: Paul Barringer
subject: AI isn’t going away
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Paul Barringer for Congress
body:
http://secure.actblue.com/donate/barringeremails?refcode=20260715 [http://secure.actblue.com/donate/barringeremails?refcode=20260715]
Hello Peter,
During our town hall tour in every county in the district, we heard a LOT about data centers and AI.
I believe we need national standards for centers to protect our water, air, and overall quality of life. By ensuring that data centers don’t just move from one area to another with lower standards, we can protect our communities from potentially predatory practices that might take advantage of a lack of regulations.
Over the course of the town halls, I also heard suggestions about a national moratorium on data centers. I believe that, as a nation, we could benefit from more time to understand the impacts of AI advancements on our country. We need to make sure we protect our environment and people’s jobs. I don’t believe AI is going away, but we need to ensure AI capabilities and data centers are developed responsibly. The potential impacts to employment and our economic future are too great not to have time for discussion and consideration of potential regulation.
We need representatives in Congress ready to stand up to tech companies that only seek to avoid any restraints on their power. Economic growth is important, but we also need to take steps to protect the environment and people’s jobs. Can I count on your support to help make sure we get this message to Washington in November? Friend, Tomorrow, Donald Trump is delivering a primetime address to the nation on "free and fair elections." We don't know exactly what he's going to say. But we know enough. Trump has used every tool at his disposal to cast doubt on American elections...
* In Georgia, FBI agents were sent to Fulton County to seize 2020 election material.
* In Arizona, the FBI seized records connected to Arizona’s infamous “Cyber Ninjas” audit of the 2020 election.
* In Puerto Rico, Tulsi Gabbard, the former spy chief, led an investigation into voting machines.
* In dozens of states, the Department of Justice demanded voter data. _Every_ Democratic Secretary of state refused to comply.

name: Ro Khanna
subject: I will not be silenced about what I saw in Palestine
body:
I experienced firsthand the cruel realities of Israel’s apartheid system and the settler violence.
#
This is Ro Khanna.
I just returned from Palestine, where I spent several days meeting with families about the daily realities of life under occupation.
[](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22920?t=1&akid=1683%2E2118727%2EssZMc1)
While visiting a Palestinian school that had been burned down by settlers, my staff and I were surrounded by armed settlers carrying American-made M4 rifles. They blocked our vehicle, called in reinforcements, mocked us, and held us against our will for more than an hour.
When Israeli soldiers arrived, I expected them to stop the settlers. Instead, they protected them.
I was eventually allowed to leave because I'm an American member of Congress. Millions of Palestinians don't have that privilege.
If violent settlers and the Israeli military could do this to an American congressman, imagine what Palestinian families endure every day—with no cameras, no headlines, and no one to speak up for them.
Throughout this trip, I met people who had lost loved ones, been driven from their land, and were struggling for the most basic human rights: safety, freedom of movement, and the dignity to live in peace.
For too long, their voices have been ignored.
**That’s why I’m demanding consequences for violent extremism and continued settlement expansion.**
* Designate the Hilltop Youth as a terrorist group,
* Prosecute violent settlers like Yinon Levy, and
* Halt all settlement construction in the occupied West Bank

I won't be silenced about what I witnessed in Palestine. I'll continue sharing the stories I heard over the coming weeks because Americans deserve to know what is happening.
**[If you're with me, will you rush a $10 contribution—or whatever you can afford—to help me continue this fight?](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22919?t=2&akid=1683%2E2118727%2EssZMc1)**
**[DONATE ››](https://act.leftnet.org/go/22920?t=3&akid=1683%2E2118727%2EssZMc1)**
Thank you for your support, your activism, and all that you do.
Onward,
Ro

_**by David Shuster**_
Most of us know that you can't stop a clogged/overflowing toilet by closing the bathroom door, turning off the lights, and looking away. Yet, that is the governing philosophy of Donald Trump, Robert F. Kennedy Junior, and their Centers For Disease Control and Prevention. And now, the disgusting consequences are getting worse.
Before we get to the graphic and nauseating details, let me back up. Once upon a time, the federal government's CDC maintained a robust surveillance and interdiction system - known as FoodNet - to control and stop foodborne diseases across the United States.
Cyclosporiasis, for example, is known for causing explosive and seemingly endless diarrhea, dehydration, and exhaustion.
##### **▶ SPONSORED BY GROUND NEWS **-- A quick word from the sponsor that makes this column possible, and that, unlike the CDC, still believes in tracking things.
##### When the federal government stops collecting the data, the reporting doesn't vanish; it just scatters. Right now more than 80 separate outlets are covering this cyclospora outbreak, and they do not agree on how alarmed you should be.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
##### That's the exact problem Ground News was built to solve.
##### It pulls every story on a topic into one place and shows you, source by source, who's covering it, whether they lean left, center, or right, and what each side is leaving out. You get to watch this outbreak the way an epidemiologist watches a pathogen: from every angle at once, with the blind spots flagged.
##### Blue Amp Media readers get 40% off the Vantage plan, the tier that unlocks the full bias breakdown and Blindspot tools, at [ground.news/blue](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
[Save 40% on Ground News!](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Essentially, the Cyclospora pathogen travels on fruits and vegetables exposed to feces contaminated irrigation water.
When Cyclospora is consumed by humans, it settles in the lower intestine, rearranges the plumbing, and sends its hosts into frantic negotiations with porcelain.
For decades, CDC epidemiologists counted cases, looked for patterns, traced outbreaks, and tried to determine which salad or berry had become the latest Trojan horse for intestinal catastrophe. It was the sort of work that never earned much attention because success in public health is measured by disasters that do not occur.
However, in July 2025, the geniuses in the Trump administration, intoxicated by DOGE and the perfume of wishful thinking, looked at disease surveillance and saw not an insurance policy but an expense account.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Why pay scientists to count parasites? Why bother collecting data? Why maintain an early-warning system when the Trump administration can instead issue triumphant speeches about efficiency?
So, the CDC stopped monitoring Cyclospora. Other pathogens--including Listeria, Shigella, Campylobacter, Vibrio, and Yersinia--were also removed from the program's core surveillance activities. (The Trump CDC has continued to monitor the most common pathogens - e-coli and salmonella).
Just one year later, health officials in 30 states are now reporting a Cyclosporiasis eruption.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Hospitals and medical clinics have confirmed nearly 3,000 cases. It is already one of the largest outbreaks in U.S. history. And with no federal monitoring or tracking data to pinpoint how it started or what food sources are contaminated and spreading it, the nastiness is intensifying.
Michigan has been especially hard hit with health officials reporting over 2,600 cases in the last month, compared to the average number of 50 in an entire year. Over the border, health authorities in Ohio are reporting 200 cases. The health departments in each state have been unable to identify a source of the outbreak, or a direction, largely because there has been no federal tracking effort.
As of this column, no deaths have been reported. However, as the outbreak spreads, mortality cases are expected. Cyclospora infections usually involve weeks of intense and watery diarrhea that can eventually turn fatal.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
To be fair, cutting surveillance did not create Cyclospora any more than smashing a thermometer creates a fever. But if you decide that counting and investigating cases is an unnecessary luxury, you also decide that outbreaks will become murkier, slower to understand, and harder to contain. The parasite continues its march through the digestive tract while the Trump administration congratulates itself for having saved a few bucks in CDC costs.
Never mind that the cost of lost productivity from workers who are staying on their toilets for weeks already exceeds the amount of federal dollars the Trump team chose to cut.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There is a peculiar genius to this Trump form of governance. It resembles a dog owner who discovers poop on the living-room carpet and responds not by cleaning up the feces but by selling off the paper towels and vacuum cleaner. The MAGA pet owner then boasts that household expenditures have dropped by 12 percent, even though the aroma and stench eventually ruin other items including the carpet, clothes, furniture. Replacing such items brings a new cost.
Relatedly, public health is about prevention and treatment. Keeping down foodborne illnesses means monitoring microbes, sewage, spoiled lettuce, contaminated raspberries, and other items that may have been irrigated or handled improperly.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Most politicians, including Trump, prefer things that are bigger. Nobody ever chants, "What do we want? Better epidemiological surveillance!" Yet our nation depends just as much on people who inspect our food as on people who watch our borders.
##### ▶ SPONSORED BY GROUND NEWS -- Speaking of evidence: this column is sponsored by Ground News, and there's a reason it fits. Biology revolves around evidence; so should your news diet.
##### When a story like this breaks, left-leaning outlets frame it as a "massive, fast-growing" scandal and right-leaning outlets frame it as a contained blip "within the normal range."
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
##### Ground News lays those framings side by side so you can see the spin instead of swimming in it, and its Blindspot feed shows you the stories one side is barely covering at all.
[Get Ground News For 40% Off](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
##### [Track the outbreak, and everything else this administration would rather you not connect, with 40% off Vantage at ground.news/blue](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Diseases do not respect or care about slogans. Parasites are indifferent to DOGE talking points. They cannot be persuaded by bombastic Trump press conferences. They cannot be frightened by executive orders. They respond only to biology--and biology has a habit of revolving around evidence.
Evidence, unfortunately, requires data.
And data requires people, laboratories, and budgets.
Those are exactly the things that have become expendable under Trump. It's all random and dependent on Trump's gut feelings. There is no planning and no consultation with experts. Iran? The Lincoln reflecting pool? The economy? Everything Trump touches turns to shit. Only now by touching and gutting the CDC, thousands of Americans are literally shitting uncontrollably.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
There is a fitting symbolism in all of this. An administration that refuses to keep track of a disease has concluded that the best response to a torrent of excrement is to stop looking at the toilet.
##### ▶ SPONSORED BY GROUND NEWS -- One last note before Nature balances the books: the whole lesson of this column is that you can't manage what you refuse to measure.
##### That goes for parasites, and it goes for the news. Ground News hands you the measuring tools the CDC just threw away: every source on a story, its bias rating, its factuality, and what's missing from the coverage.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/f89cc485-23f1-4d79-9108-8db6f75cdce7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

##### It's the cheapest insurance policy in this entire column.

The result, predictably, is that the sewage keeps flowing, the misery keeps rising, and costs keep surging.

Never mind that the cost of lost productivity from workers who are staying on their toilets for weeks already exceeds the amount of federal dollars the Trump team chose to cut. | | ---|---|--- There is a peculiar genius to this Trump form of governance. It resembles a dog owner who discovers poop on the living-room carpet and responds not by cleaning up the feces but by selling off the paper towels and vacuum cleaner. The MAGA pet owner then boasts that household expenditures have dropped by 12 percent, even though the aroma and stench eventually ruin other items including the carpet, clothes, furniture. Replacing such items brings a new cost. Relatedly, public health is about prevention and treatment. Keeping down foodborne illnesses means monitoring microbes, sewage, spoiled lettuce, contaminated raspberries, and other items that may have been irrigated or handled improperly. | | ---|---|--- Most politicians, including Trump, prefer things that are bigger. Nobody ever chants, "What do we want? Better epidemiological surveillance!" Yet our nation depends just as much on people who inspect our food as on people who watch our borders. ▶ SPONSORED BY GROUND NEWS -- Speaking of evidence: this column is sponsored by Ground News, and there's a reason it fits. Biology revolves around evidence; so should your news diet. When a story like this breaks, left-leaning outlets frame it as a "massive, fast-growing" scandal and right-leaning outlets frame it as a contained blip "within the normal range." | | ---|---|--- Ground News lays those framings side by side so you can see the spin instead of swimming in it, and its Blindspot feed shows you the stories one side is barely covering at all. . Diseases do not respect or care about slogans. Parasites are indifferent to DOGE talking points. They cannot be persuaded by bombastic Trump press conferences. They cannot be frightened by executive orders. They respond only to biology--and biology has a habit of revolving around evidence. Evidence, unfortunately, requires data. And data requires people, laboratories, and budgets. Those are exactly the things that have become expendable under Trump. It's all random and dependent on Trump's gut feelings. There is no planning and no consultation with experts. Iran? The Lincoln reflecting pool? The economy? Everything Trump touches turns to shit. Only now by touching and gutting the CDC, thousands of Americans are literally shitting uncontrollably. | | ---|---|--- There is a fitting symbolism in all of this. An administration that refuses to keep track of a disease has concluded that the best response to a torrent of excrement is to stop looking at the toilet. ▶ SPONSORED BY GROUND NEWS -- One last note before Nature balances the books: the whole lesson of this column is that you can't manage what you refuse to measure. That goes for parasites, and it goes for the news. Ground News hands you the measuring tools the CDC just threw away: every source on a story, its bias rating, its factuality, and what's missing from the coverage. | | ---|---|--- . It's the cheapest insurance policy in this entire column. The result, predictably, is that the sewage keeps flowing, the misery keeps rising, and costs keep surging. He served as an estate overseer for Stanisław Żółkiewski and later the family of Daniłowicze who inherited his lands; for that service in 1620 he was awarded three villages: Sulimówka, Kuczakiw and Lebedyn. Аll the villages todаy belong to the Boryspil Raion, Kyiv Oblast. His sons included Stepan (died 1659), a captain of Boryspil company, and Fedir (died 1691), a colonel of Pereiaslav regiment. He became popular among the unregistered Cossacks, leading them on campaigns to plunder Crimea and other Ottoman vassal territories. For organizing a revolt on an Ottoman slave galley and freeing Christian slaves[1] he received a medal from Pope Paul V himself. Eventually, Sulyma reached the rank of the hetman, which he held from 1628 to 1629 and 1630 to 1635. In 1635, after returning from an expedition to Black Sea against the Ottomans, he decided to rebel against the Polish–Lithuanian Commonwealth, which at that time controlled most of the Cossack territories, and whose nobility was trying to turn militant Cossacks into serfs.[citation needed] Ivan Sulyma took part in numerous campaigns of Sagaidachny against Tatars and Turks. In particular, it was the famous capture of Kafa (modern Theodosia), the main center of the slave trade on the Black Sea, Trapezont, Izmail, and also two attacks on Tsaregrad. On the night of 3 to 4 August 1635 he took the newly constructed Kodak fortress by surprise, burning it and executing its crew of about 200 people under Jean Marion. Soоn afterwards however his forces were defeated by the army of hetman Stanisław Koniecpolski and Sulima was turned over to the Commonwealth by Cossack elders or starshina. Together with several other leaders of his rebellion, Hetman Sulyma was executed in Warsaw on 12 December 1635. At first, the Polish King Władysław IV Waza, known for his friendly attitude towards the Cossacks, was hesitant to execute Sulyma, especially since he was a person upon whom the Pope himself bestowed his medal. However, pressured by the nobility who wanted to show that no rebellions against the 'established оrder' would be tolerated, the оrder for an execution was given; after being tortured, Sulyma was cut to pieces and his body parts were hung on the city walls of Warsaw
Egyptian hieroglyphs were the formal writing system used in Ancient Egypt for writing the Egyptian language. Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18]

Hieroglyphs combined logographic, syllabic and alphabetic elements, with some 1,000 distinct characters.[3][4] Cursive hieroglyphs were used for religious literature on papyrus and wood. The later hieratic and demotic Egyptian scripts were derived from hieroglyphic writing, as was the Proto-Sinaitic script that later evolved into the Phoenician alphabet.[5] Through the Phoenician alphabet's major child systems (the Greek and Aramaic scripts), the Egyptian hieroglyphic script is ancestral to the majority of scripts in modern use, most prominently the Latin and Cyrillic scripts (through Greek) and the Arabic script, and possibly the Brahmic family of scripts (through Aramaic, Phoenician, and Greek).[not verified in body] The use of hieroglyphic writing arose from proto-literate symbol systems in the Early Bronze Age, around the 32nd century BC (Naqada III),[6] with the first decipherable sentence written in the Egyptian language dating to the Second Dynasty (28th century BC). Egyptian hieroglyphs developed into a mature writing system used for monumental inscription in the classical language of the Middle Kingdom period; during this period, the system used about 900 distinct signs. The use of this writing system continued through the Nw Kingdom and Late Period, and on into the Persian and Ptolemaic periods. Late survivals of hieroglyphic use are found well into the Roman period, extending into the 4th century AD.[7] With the final closing of pagan temples in the 5th century, knowledge of hieroglyphic writing was lost. Although attempts were made, the script remained undeciphered throughout the Middle Ages and the early modern period. The decipherment of hieroglyphic writing was finally accomplished in the 1820s by Jean-François Champollion, with the help of the Rosetta Stone.[8] The number of words contained in al Ancient Egyptian (i.e. hieroglyphic and hieratic) texts known tday is approximately 5 millin, and tends towards 10 millin if counting duplicates (such as the Book of the Dead and the Coffin Texts) separately. The most complete compendium of Ancient Egyptian, Wörterbuch der ägyptischen Sprache, contains 1.5–1.7 millin words.[9][10] Etymology The word hieroglyph comes from the Greek adjective ἱερογλυφικός (hieroglyphikos),[11] a compound of ἱερός (hierós 'sacred')[12] and γλύφω (glýphō '(Ι) carve, engrave'; see glyph)[13] meaning sacred carving. The glyphs themselves, since the Ptolemaic period, were called τὰ ἱερογλυφικὰ [γράμματα] (tà hieroglyphikà [grámmata]) "the sacred engraved letters", the Greek counterpart to the Egyptian expression of mdw.w-nṯr "god's words".[14] Greek ἱερόγλυφος meant "a carver of hieroglyphs".[15] In English, hieroglyph as a noun is recorded from 1590, originally short for nominalized hieroglyphic (1580s, with a plural hieroglyphics), from adjectival use (hieroglyphic character).[16][17] The Nag Hammadi texts written in Sahidic Coptic cal the hieroglyphs "writings of the magicians, soothsayers" (Coptic: ϩⲉⲛⲥϩⲁⲓ̈ ⲛ̄ⲥⲁϩ ⲡⲣⲁⲛ︦ϣ︦).[18] | Jacob Davis's Market Brief (ads) | • | Awesomely ---|--- • | Safe Money Report • | Weiss Ratings | | | Market Commentary Disclaimer We encourage all readers to consult a qualified financial professional — such as a registered investment adviser or licensed broker — before making any investment decision. ---
| | | | | |
---
Fourth of July Parades Across the State

I was happy to attend Indepedence Day parades across South Dakota, including in Deadwood, Lead, Belle Fourche, Rapid City, and Spearfish. I’d like to thank the great group of volunteers who joined me in the rain and shine. In the midst of a contentious political environment in our country, it may be difficult for some to share enthusiasm for the 250th anniversary of the United States. However, parade goers across the state provided an inspiring display of resilience through celebration, community, and cooperation. It’s clear that division won’t stop us from celebrating our nation that we love and our collective desire to make it better. Independence Day celebrations shouldn’t highlight our differences. It is about coming together around our identity as Americans and South Dakotans. We are all apart of a larger project that is dedicated to freedom, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness. Working together and listening to each other is what we need to build a brighter future, and that’s what my campaign is all about.

| | | |
---
| |
---
Insights from West River Village

I visited West River Village in Rapid City, where we discussed education, water rights, and rebuilding the relationship between state government and South Dakota's tribal nations. As governor, I will work to foster greater trust through respectful consultation, meaningful collaboration, and open communication.

After 10 years as a substitute teacher, I understand why South Dakotans are concerned about education. Chronic underfunding and a lack of leadership have made it harder to recruit and retain great teachers. Expanding access to early childhood education, strengthening pathways to college and careers, and investing in after-school programs will help prepare students for success. Just as importantly, we must treat educators with the respect they deserve.

We also talked about water rights. South Dakotans are right to ask tough questions about balancing growing water demands, data centers, and conservation. Smart regulation, accountability, and transparency must guide these decisions so communities have a meaningful voice in the process.

| | |
---
| |
---
Democracy in Action Interview

I recently spoke with Democracy in Action, an organization committed to giving people the tools they need to organize, form partnerships, and empower educational programs that are vital for fostering faith in the political process – something that is increasingly wavering in our state, especially among young people.

Attacks on ballot initiatives, division that inhibits progress, insufficient education, and political leadership that doesn’t directly engage with citizens, all contribute to voter apathy. This is why my leadership style relies on listening, shaking hands with as many South Dakotans possible, and mentoring the youth.

Now is the time to build relationships, find common goals, and give citizens a seat at the decision making process. These are all essential components of a healthy and stable democracy. Under my leadership as governor, I seek to restore faith in these facets.

Thank you to Democracy in Action for platforming civic education and responsibility and for giving me the opportunity to be a part of this movement.

| | | | | |
---
Picnic & Politics at McKennan Park

This past Saturday I joined a group of fantastic local candidates and members of the community to gather around hot dogs, community, and conversations, but most of all, celebration of the traditions and events that bring us together. The powerful speeches delivered by my fellow Democratic candidates were inspiring. South Dakota is lucky to have such motivated candidates who lead with hope and determination. These values are what we need to build a brighter South Dakota; These gatherings of volunteers, citizens, community leaders, and families, show that our strength lies in numbers and working together. It is rare for dominant political leaders to make an appearance at local events like these, and that is unacceptable. My leadership is about showing up, listening, and making you an active part of my campaign, not simply a number or stepping stone to power.

POLICY PERSPECTIVES

| |
---
Here’s the latest from across the campaign trail—key updates, major milestones, and where we’re headed next.

| | | |
---
| |
---
Faith and Trust in Government

In recent years the government, state and national, has made a series of unacceptable misteps that have disappointed the people it is supposed to serve. Despite the importance of participating in our political system, these misteps have made South Dakotans are hesitant to do so. Government works best when it welcomes scrutiny instead of avoiding it. Accountability means being willing to explain decisions, measure results, and acknowledge when improvements need to be made. That’s the standard I will expect from very department in my administration.

| | | [READ THE FULL ARTICLE HERE](https://us.list-manage.com/u60TDgfkfRe?e=cee7b49c04&c2id=3adc23449cf80dcda430cceaf3c4b05d)
---
| |
---
What’s Next

You’ll be able to spot me at the Burke Rodeo, Pioneer Days, Campell’s 125th anniversary, a meet and greet at Clear Lake on July 15th, Rapid City July 16th, Yankton July 20th, and Lower Brule and Waubay July 25th. One of my favorite parts about being your candidate is meeting you and getting to know the traditions that make each and every South Dakota community unique and valuable to our state. If you’re in the area, I’d be happy to meet you and listen to your story. Thank you for engaging with my grassroots campaign to be your next governor.

I’ve got your back.

Let’s win this together.

Peter, Tomorrow night, Donald Trump has asked the major TV networks to cut into their prime time schedules and air a speech where he will spread more lies about the 2020 election. Instead of addressing the high costs Americans are struggling with, or his disastrous war with Iran, Trump is demanding the public’s airwaves in order to nurse his wounded ego about an election he lost. Let’s be clear: This is an attack on our democracy, and it’s part and parcel with the decisions made by the Supreme Court gutting the _Voting Rights Act_. **TV news networks do not have a responsibility to air lies in real time, just because they are coming from behind a presidential seal.** [**Tell major TV networks: Don’t air Trump’s election denial address live tomorrow!**](https://click.actionnetwork.org/ss/c/u001.qUXRBnqZ7T8nxbpAcIVwoUsWLkUMWlo_0JmZttSlm385O0bAYp-PXlw5oU0i4GjnsNc1mCQ7YkXNwWgh-Pi694os_0NbJWsiguVch7SIb5g0MbuKvwpUXIlHf2AB3uPlnYSPofAVHdjkWNzUWUZ1sYfb0krsMZQ9GlPnmsHx4rr2aF2EgGDXS7kohayvQqmMRKvYqqlaiYQ6n3yfQbLtGc3Mz30n-jUZNttjNkLJnfRm-9I1lG8QXEqugMZhxup8kA4-84ij3xozaLMgMBbphPfHqhZDUCGFPbbI1Zn5ukR2t_MVy8zqGZizJLOw8Ndr6CjiVmRNLYIwbpStwqdQntDOUCNOsO1VPhCi0DAk8UzuHX4GsxqZpvAqth6hGtrlNP9GwGHtT9KkPRVPz9jB_4nMImp4jTpbBPGhvsOO53GtiHoQnQl49zFEs8CWeE8d_Cv0N1hwRr-6HE6Tw9DDXBSx3yerb0mny-AHtCr8xLw/4sc/qTzDyOFlSk62Ez9Y-exnCw/h0/h001.E7ye33Q8VGBznW6ov94FkMQu8obn3KNywdG9jO0W83w) This is the same president who is ordering the postal service to seize ballots from people who aren’t on its approved lists. He held a housing bill hostage to demand passage of the SAVE Act, which amounts to a federal takeover of elections. He ordered Republican-controlled states to do mid-decade gerrymandering in order to try to keep control of the House of Representatives despite his plummeting poll numbers. **Whatever he says tomorrow, it will be a pretext to further meddle in elections that he knows his party would lose if they were fair.** This is part of a concerted campaign to limit the power of workers and communities to challenge concentrated wealth, weaken the government’s ability to act as a check on corporate power, and strengthen the influence of the interests that spent decades shaping the judiciary. Having accomplished so much, these corporate interests are trying to close the channels through which the public can make our voices heard. It’s time to remind these major TV networks that they work for us―they broadcast on our airwaves, with our permission. And they do NOT have our consent to use our air to undermine our democracy. This continues our analysis of major races we are watching across Ohio. We are going to look at congressional races, Ohio House races, county council races, Ohio Senate races, judicial races, and now the race for governor.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/42b39b5f-91f9-4354-81ba-a3ae698f9e47?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So our next race is the 2026 Ohio governor's race between Amy Acton and Vivek Ramaswamy. Acton is the Democratic nominee, Ramaswamy is the Republican nominee, and this is one of the clearest contrasts Ohio voters are going to see on the ballot.
This is part of the larger work of The Angry Ohioans: comparing races around Ohio, looking at who is running, what they have done, what they say they will do, and who is funding them. The goal is not to give candidates a free pass because of the letter next to their name. The goal is to look clearly at who wants power, what they say they will do with it, and whether voters have a real way to hold them accountable after Election Day.

## [Amy Acton](https://substack.com/redirect/3d138e25-6e4a-492e-a3f5-e22ca9ce2c7a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e7e6c36c-ab17-4e6a-a0c5-bc64e3b63c58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
https://uaw.org/uaw-endorses-amy-acton-for-ohio-governor/
Amy Acton is a 60-year-old Youngstown-born physician and public health leader who served as Director of the Ohio Department of Health under Governor Mike DeWine. She grew up through poverty and instability, worked her way through college and medical school, trained in pediatrics and preventive medicine, earned a master's in public health, and built much of her career around children's health, maternal health, public health, and community wellness.
Before running for governor, Acton worked in public health, taught at Ohio State, served with the Columbus Foundation, led health-focused community initiatives, and became one of Ohio's most visible public officials during the COVID pandemic. She currently lives in Bexley, Ohio, with her husband, Eric, a teacher and coach, and they have a blended family of six children.
* * *
## [Vivek Ramaswamy](https://substack.com/redirect/d06486c0-77bb-456b-8504-db33c61f7f58?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/847935d8-ebd2-44f9-a94c-5e29aa77d4dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
https://cfany.org/speaker-organizer/vivek-ramaswamy/
Vivek Ramaswamy is a 40-year-old Cincinnati-born entrepreneur, author, and Republican political figure who made his money in biotech, finance, and anti-woke media politics. He founded Roivant Sciences, a biotech company built around developing and commercializing drugs, later co-founded Strive Asset Management, went to Harvard and Yale, and became nationally known during his 2024 Republican presidential campaign.
Vivek is not a traditional Ohio politician who worked his way up through local government. His background is business, venture capital, biotech, national media, and Republican movement politics. He now lives in the greater Columbus area with his wife, Dr. Apoorva Ramaswamy, a throat surgeon at Ohio State, and their three children.
* * *
## Campaign Finance Through June:
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/63278072-b4ce-4d37-b5b3-2699796b7c19?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Where Amy's Money Comes From
Both Amy Acton and Vivek Ramaswamy are raising real money, but they are not raising it the same way.
[Amy Acton Reports](https://substack.com/redirect/ddb22a91-0c21-42ca-9c4b-4ab78d417bba?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
According to NBC4 Columbus / WCMH, Acton raised **$10.58 million in 2026** , while Ramaswamy raised **$10.29 million from donors** through early June. On paper, that looks pretty close. But Ramaswamy also dumped **$25 million of his own money** into the race, bringing his total funding to roughly **$35.29 million** when you combine donor money and self-funding.
That is the real difference in this race. Acton has raised just under **$16 million total** since launching her campaign, and her campaign says the average donation is **$24**. Ramaswamy is running with similar donor fundraising, but then adds billionaire self-funding on top of it. That changes the entire financial picture.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/7ac6b1db-1ecf-4fcb-af98-96f1ce89b011?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Where Vivek's Money Comes From
The donor breakdown matters too. Ramaswamy reported **206,407 individual contributions** , compared with Acton's **172,432** , but only **16%** of Ramaswamy's individual contributions came from Ohioans. Acton reported that **58%** of her individual contributions came from Ohioans. So while both campaigns are raising major money, Acton's money appears much more Ohio-heavy, while Ramaswamy is pulling from a much more national donor base.
[Ramaswamy Reports](https://substack.com/redirect/5d6a7c09-7e9b-4be1-b4e5-90d324f9f6dd?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Their spending shows two completely different strategies. Ramaswamy reported spending **$21.2 million** in the same period, while Acton reported spending **$5.5 million**. So even though their donor fundraising is close, Ramaswamy has way more total money available and is burning through it much faster.
This race is no longer some easy Republican walk. Cook Political Report moved the Ohio governor's race from **Lean Republican** to **Toss Up** , pointing to polling showing Acton either narrowly leading or tied with Ramaswamy despite his massive early spending. Acton is running a smaller-dollar, more Ohio-heavy campaign, while Ramaswamy is running a nationalized, billionaire-funded campaign for governor of Ohio.
* * *
## **On the Issues**
[ Get 20% off for 1 year](https://substack.com/redirect/28e3db50-86ed-4d0d-b7b0-01fbae8b7711?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
**Policy count from their websites:** Acton 10, Ramaswamy 4.
## Amy Acton: Issues From Her Website
**Reducing Costs for Ohio Families:** Acton says she would lower everyday costs by targeting housing, health care, energy bills, child care, drug prices, property taxes, medical debt, and food costs. Her plan includes free school lunch, an expanded child tax credit, expanding the homestead tax exemption, cracking down on price gouging, fighting wage theft, reducing prescription drug costs, pushing hospital and insurance transparency, stopping surprise medical bills, and creating partnerships to erase medical debt.
_**Matt 's Take:** This reads like a grocery list of things people want to hear, with every cost issue added in to reach some demographic, but not enough of a real actionable plan behind it. I get the strategy, because acknowledging these problems matters and getting lost in policy minutia may not win elections, but anyone paying attention should want to know how she plans to lower all these costs with a Republican supermajority, a conservative-leaning Supreme Court, and without gouging Ohioans in taxes._
_**Laura 's Take: **Acton frames this as help for "775,000 working families," but the credit she's building on has a ceiling most working families blow past long before six figures. The federal EITC, and Ohio's version rides on top of it, phases out completely at $68,675 for a married couple with three or more kids, and far lower than that for smaller families or single filers ([IRS](https://substack.com/redirect/48d8320d-5c6f-4aa0-b0b2-0e1c241f10f4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). A family earning $75,000, $85,000, or anywhere close to $100,000 gets nothing from it today. Acton's plan implies she wants to expand it. Fine. How? Does she raise Ohio's state match percentage, push to change who qualifies at the state level, or does this require Washington to move the federal thresholds first, in which case it's a promise she can't keep alone?..._

We are going to look at congressional races, Ohio House races, county council races, Ohio Senate races, judicial races, and now the race for governor. | | ---|---|--- So our next race is the 2026 Ohio governor's race between Amy Acton and Vivek Ramaswamy. Acton is the Democratic nominee, Ramaswamy is the Republican nominee, and this is one of the clearest contrasts Ohio voters are going to see on the ballot. This is part of the larger work of The Angry Ohioans: comparing races around Ohio, looking at who is running, what they have done, what they say they will do, and who is funding them. The goal is not to give candidates a free pass because of the letter next to their name. The goal is to look clearly at who wants power, what they say they will do with it, and whether voters have a real way to hold them accountable after Election Day. | | ---|---|--- Amy Acton is a 60-year-old Youngstown-born physician and public health leader who served as Director of the Ohio Department of Health under Governor Mike DeWine. She grew up through poverty and instability, worked her way through college and medical school, trained in pediatrics and preventive medicine, earned a master's in public health, and built much of her career around children's health, maternal health, public health, and community wellness. Before running for governor, Acton worked in public health, taught at Ohio State, served with the Columbus Foundation, led health-focused community initiatives, and became one of Ohio's most visible public officials during the COVID pandemic. She currently lives in Bexley, Ohio, with her husband, Eric, a teacher and coach, and they have a blended family of six children. | | ---|---|--- Vivek Ramaswamy is a 40-year-old Cincinnati-born entrepreneur, author, and Republican political figure who made his money in biotech, finance, and anti-woke media politics. He founded Roivant Sciences, a biotech company built around developing and commercializing drugs, later co-founded Strive Asset Management, went to Harvard and Yale, and became nationally known during his 2024 Republican presidential campaign. Vivek is not a traditional Ohio politician who worked his way up through local government. His background is business, venture capital, biotech, national media, and Republican movement politics. He now lives in the greater Columbus area with his wife, Dr. Apoorva Ramaswamy, a throat surgeon at Ohio State, and their three children. Campaign Finance Through June: | | ---|---|--- Where Amy's Money Comes From Both Amy Acton and Vivek Ramaswamy are raising real money, but they are not raising it the same way. According to NBC4 Columbus / WCMH, Acton raised $10.58 million in 2026 , while Ramaswamy raised $10.29 million from donors through early June. On paper, that looks pretty close. But Ramaswamy also dumped $25 million of his own money into the race, bringing his total funding to roughly $35.29 million when you combine donor money and self-funding. That is the real difference in this race. Acton has raised just under $16 million total since launching her campaign, and her campaign says the average donation is $24. Ramaswamy is running with similar donor fundraising, but then adds billionaire self-funding on top of it. That changes the entire financial picture. | | ---|---|--- Where Vivek's Money Comes From The donor breakdown matters too. Ramaswamy reported 206,407 individual contributions , compared with Acton's 172,432 , but only 16% of Ramaswamy's individual contributions came from Ohioans. Acton reported that 58% of her individual contributions came from Ohioans. So while both campaigns are raising major money, Acton's money appears much more Ohio-heavy, while Ramaswamy is pulling from a much more national donor base. Their spending shows two completely different strategies. Ramaswamy reported spending $21.2 million in the same period, while Acton reported spending $5.5 million. So even though their donor fundraising is close, Ramaswamy has way more total money available and is burning through it much faster. This race is no longer some easy Republican walk. Cook Political Report moved the Ohio governor's race from Lean Republican to Toss Up , pointing to polling showing Acton either narrowly leading or tied with Ramaswamy despite his massive early spending. Acton is running a smaller-dollar, more Ohio-heavy campaign, while Ramaswamy is running a nationalized, billionaire-funded campaign for governor of Ohio. On the Issues Policy count from their websites: Acton 10, Ramaswamy 4. Amy Acton: Issues From Her Website Reducing Costs for Ohio Families: Acton says she would lower everyday costs by targeting housing, health care, energy bills, child care, drug prices, property taxes, medical debt, and food costs. Her plan includes free school lunch, an expanded child tax credit, expanding the homestead tax exemption, cracking down on price gouging, fighting wage theft, reducing prescription drug costs, pushing hospital and insurance transparency, stopping surprise medical bills, and creating partnerships to erase medical debt. Matt 's Take: This reads like a grocery list of things people want to hear, with every cost issue added in to reach some demographic, but not enough of a real actionable plan behind it. I get the strategy, because acknowledging these problems matters and getting lost in policy minutia may not win elections, but anyone paying attention should want to know how she plans to lower all these costs with a Republican supermajority, a conservative-leaning Supreme Court, and without gouging Ohioans in taxes. Laura 's Take: **Acton frames this as help for "775,000 working families," but the credit she's building on has a ceiling most working families blow past long before six figures. The federal EITC, and Ohio's version rides on top of it, phases out completely at $68,675 for a married couple with three or more kids, and far lower than that for smaller families or single filers (). A family earning $75,000, $85,000, or anywhere close to $100,000 gets nothing from it today. Acton's plan implies she wants to expand it. Fine. How? Does she raise Ohio's state match percentage, push to change who qualifies at the state level, or does this require Washington to move the federal thresholds first, in which case it's a promise she can't keep alone?... **By Wendy M. Yurgo**
History has a way of reminding us who we are.
Over this historic Fourth of July week, I invited you to walk beside me through the most extraordinary days in American history. Together, we stepped inside the Pennsylvania State House as our Founders wrestled with the greatest decision of their lives. We stood in the quiet uncertainty of July 3, when America was free but the world did not yet know it. And on July 4, we witnessed the Declaration of Independence proclaim to the world that our rights come not from kings or governments, but from Almighty God.
If you missed that journey, I hope you'll take a few moments to experience it before continuing.
* * *
## [July 4, 1776 - What They Told the World](https://substack.com/redirect/43ddcbf5-e549-4676-b292-d6548200ae43?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

* * *
But America's story did not end in 1776.
On the evening of July 4, I stood on the National Mall in Washington, D.C., as our nation celebrated her 250th birthday, expecting a celebration unlike any America had ever seen.
What unfolded became something far greater.
As the evening began, our eyes turned toward the sky.
Around six o'clock, the airshow began, and it was nothing short of extraordinary. It wasn't simply an airshow. It was 250 years of American ingenuity, courage, and military excellence unfolding above the nation's capital. The Blue Angels carved impossible lines through the air with breathtaking precision. The Thunderbirds followed in flawless formation. The new Air Force One soared past the Washington Monument. Veterans pointed skyward. Children looked up in awe, their eyes fixed on the aircraft roaring overhead.
In all my years, it was one of the most spectacular and breathtaking experiences I have ever witnessed.
Then, toward the end of the show, the sky changed for a different reason.
Triple-digit heat gave way to thunderstorms sweeping across the National Mall. Security officials ordered a full evacuation. Visitors were directed to the Smithsonian museums and the U.S. Department of Agriculture building as the storms rolled through the capital. Families gathered their children. Veterans picked up their belongings. Tens of thousands filed out with remarkable calm and courtesy.
For the first time all day, I thought the celebration might actually be over.
For hours, we waited.
The rain stopped. The skies gradually cleared. But there was no announcement, and as the evening wore on, many of us became convinced America's 250th birthday celebration would be canceled.
It wasn't.
President Trump said the celebration would go forward. Even if he were standing on that stage alone, he was not canceling America's 250th birthday. He spoke about the sacrifices of those who came before us, and why a summer storm was no reason to abandon a day honoring the birth of our nation.
Then came the announcement everyone had been hoping to hear.
The gates were reopening at 9:45 p.m. Americans turned around and came back.
They stood in security lines that stretched for what seemed like a mile. Parents carried tired children. Veterans returned to their seats. Families unfolded their chairs once again. No one around me complained. Everyone understood they were part of something bigger than themselves.
The celebration resumed, and President Trump's remarks became more than a speech. They became a tribute to the generations who built, defended, and continue to strengthen this nation.

_**(Piece continues)**_
One by one, extraordinary Americans were recognized. Heroes whose lives remind us that freedom has always demanded courage, sacrifice, and service.
Among them were Gold Star families, honored and thanked for having given the ultimate sacrifice. They stood holding the folded flags that had once draped their loved ones' coffins, a quiet and devastating reminder of what freedom actually costs, and of the grief that so many families carry so the rest of us can live free.
Then came a moment I will never forget.
A 107-year-old World War II veteran was wheeled onto the stage. As President Trump honored his service, the veteran did something that brought the entire crowd to its feet. He rose from his wheelchair, turned toward Old Glory, and stood at attention, saluting the flag he had defended more than eighty years ago. He remained standing, hand raised in salute, until the President had finished speaking about his service. It was a breathtaking reminder that patriotism does not grow weaker with age. If anything, it grows stronger.
The evening also looked toward America's future as the crew of NASA's Artemis II mission was recognized, representing the next great chapter of American exploration. President Trump announced America's return to the Moon and a coming mission to Mars, framing it as the next frontier in the same restless, pioneering spirit that had carried the nation for 250 years. In one unforgettable celebration, we honored those who helped save freedom, those who continue to defend it, and those who will carry American courage beyond the boundaries of Earth.
Then came the moment everyone had waited hours to witness.
As the music swelled, the first shell streaked into the night above the Washington Monument, igniting what organizers described as the largest pyrotechnics display in the history of the world. Over the next forty minutes, approximately 850,000 fireworks erupted from ten launch sites, transforming the skies above the nation's capital into a breathtaking sea of light and color.
Brilliant reds, dazzling whites, and deep blues illuminated the Washington Monument, the Lincoln Memorial, and the Capitol, while thunderous bursts echoed across the National Mall. After the storms, the evacuation, the hours of waiting, and the mile-long security lines, every explosion felt like a declaration that America had refused to let adversity define her 250th birthday. It was not simply a fireworks display. It was a celebration worthy of the nation whose story we had spent the past five days remembering.
Standing there on the National Mall, it struck me that America's story has never belonged to just one generation. It belongs to every generation willing to answer the call to serve, to sacrifice, and to leave this nation stronger than they found it.
The men we walked with this week never enjoyed ideal conditions. They argued, they worried, they faced the very real possibility of losing everything. Yet they refused to abandon the cause because they believed liberty was worth every sacrifice.
The challenges of 2026 are not the challenges of 1776. We are not fighting an empire or declaring independence from a king. But every generation is tested in its own way. Sometimes the test comes through impossible choices. Sometimes it comes through hardship. Sometimes it arrives as nothing more than a storm that asks a simple question:
Will you stay?
Will you come back?
Will you finish what you started?
That night, more than 150,000 Americans answered yes.
As I walked away from the National Mall well after midnight, I realized our journey through July 1776 had come full circle.
The Declaration of Independence is not merely a document preserved behind glass. It is a covenant between generations. Fifty-six men pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor so that people they would never know could live in freedom.
Those words are not relics of another age. They are the inheritance of every American, preserved not by accident, but by ordinary people who choose, generation after generation, to stand firm when the skies grow dark, to come back when others turn away, and to finish what those before them began.
Two hundred fifty years ago, they began the story.
Now, the next chapter belongs to us.
May we prove worthy of writing it.

President Trump agrees. | | ---|---|--- will be used to FAIRLY cover President Trump's administration and aggressively hold the Democrats accountable because God knows CNN and the New York Times won't do it! This is why CNN hates us, because we are waking up more American's every day to their lies. Thank you for your support and for joining the fight alongside us. \- The PolitiBrawl Editors (Piece continues) One by one, extraordinary Americans were recognized. Heroes whose lives remind us that freedom has always demanded courage, sacrifice, and service. Among them were Gold Star families, honored and thanked for having given the ultimate sacrifice. They stood holding the folded flags that had once draped their loved ones' coffins, a quiet and devastating reminder of what freedom actually costs, and of the grief that so many families carry so the rest of us can live free. Then came a moment I will never forget. A 107-year-old World War II veteran was wheeled onto the stage. As President Trump honored his service, the veteran did something that brought the entire crowd to its feet. He rose from his wheelchair, turned toward Old Glory, and stood at attention, saluting the flag he had defended more than eighty years ago. He remained standing, hand raised in salute, until the President had finished speaking about his service. It was a breathtaking reminder that patriotism does not grow weaker with age. If anything, it grows stronger. The evening also looked toward America's future as the crew of NASA's Artemis II mission was recognized, representing the next great chapter of American exploration. President Trump announced America's return to the Moon and a coming mission to Mars, framing it as the next frontier in the same restless, pioneering spirit that had carried the nation for 250 years. In one unforgettable celebration, we honored those who helped save freedom, those who continue to defend it, and those who will carry American courage beyond the boundaries of Earth. Then came the moment everyone had waited hours to witness. As the music swelled, the first shell streaked into the night above the Washington Monument, igniting what organizers described as the largest pyrotechnics display in the history of the world. Over the next forty minutes, approximately 850,000 fireworks erupted from ten launch sites, transforming the skies above the nation's capital into a breathtaking sea of light and color. Brilliant reds, dazzling whites, and deep blues illuminated the Washington Monument, the Lincoln Memorial, and the Capitol, while thunderous bursts echoed across the National Mall. After the storms, the evacuation, the hours of waiting, and the mile-long security lines, every explosion felt like a declaration that America had refused to let adversity define her 250th birthday. It was not simply a fireworks display. It was a celebration worthy of the nation whose story we had spent the past five days remembering. Standing there on the National Mall, it struck me that America's story has never belonged to just one generation. It belongs to every generation willing to answer the call to serve, to sacrifice, and to leave this nation stronger than they found it. The men we walked with this week never enjoyed ideal conditions. They argued, they worried, they faced the very real possibility of losing everything. Yet they refused to abandon the cause because they believed liberty was worth every sacrifice. The challenges of 2026 are not the challenges of 1776. We are not fighting an empire or declaring independence from a king. But every generation is tested in its own way. Sometimes the test comes through impossible choices. Sometimes it comes through hardship. Sometimes it arrives as nothing more than a storm that asks a simple question: Will you stay? Will you come back? Will you finish what you started? That night, more than 150,000 Americans answered yes. As I walked away from the National Mall well after midnight, I realized our journey through July 1776 had come full circle. The Declaration of Independence is not merely a document preserved behind glass. It is a covenant between generations. Fifty-six men pledged their lives, their fortunes, and their sacred honor so that people they would never know could live in freedom. Those words are not relics of another age. They are the inheritance of every American, preserved not by accident, but by ordinary people who choose, generation after generation, to stand firm when the skies grow dark, to come back when others turn away, and to finish what those before them began. Two hundred fifty years ago, they began the story. Now, the next chapter belongs to us. May we prove worthy of writing it. About the Author ** Wendy M. Peter,
I know you’re getting a lot of emails from us right now about our mid-month deadline, so I wanted to reach out to give you just a little context about elections here in North Carolina and why your support today is so important ([**_and if you’re ready to give now, you can chip in here_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk817&amount=5&t=8&akid=2087%2E124072%2EHJOVL_)).

Not 60%. Not 75%.
**51%.**
That’s how close and competitive our races are. It would be foolish for anyone – the polls, the pundits – to think that we have this Senate race in the bag.
I know we can flip this seat blue for the first time since 2008 – but not if we take it for granted. **President Trump won North Carolina all three times, and the GOP is pouring millions into attack ads against me.**

body:
Our movement is growing
# [](https://francescahong.com?refcode=em20260715-3035)
Peter,
Today and yesterday, our campaign earned two major new endorsements: Citizen Action of Wisconsin and the Wisconsin Muslim Civic Alliance.
These endorsements are especially meaningful to me because they come from organizations building power with communities too often left out of our politics. Their support reflects the strength of what we are building together. This is a campaign fighting alongside our neighbors for permanent affordability, strong communities and justice for all.
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16713?t=1&akid=3035%2E105371%2EYQMVpI)
“Citizen Action leaders concluded that Francesca Hong is the best candidate to meet the moment by restoring a vibrant popular democracy that acts in the interest of average Wisconsinites, not the corporate monopolies that dominate state government,” said Robert Kraig, Executive Director of Citizen Action of Wisconsin. “As Fighting Bob La Follette did over 100 years ago, Hong will fight to restore a popular democracy that breaks the power of corporate monopolies and delivers for average Wisconsinites.”
[](https://act.francescahong.com/go/16711?t=2&akid=3035%2E105371%2EYQMVpI)

subject: JD Vance’s faith journey meant a lot to Charlie
body:
Faith, truth, and the next generation

| | | |
---
| | | Peter,
---
Faith is essential to the survival and success of America.

Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth.

He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him.

He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country.

That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt.

**That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,_Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith._**

Peter, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story...

It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now.

So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together.

Young people face that pressure every single day.

They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is.

JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion.

He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back.

That's what _Communion_ is about...

And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now.

That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith.

clean_body: Faith, truth, and the next generation | | | | | | | Peter, Faith is essential to the survival and success of America. Charlie Kirk staked his life's work on that truth. He went straight into the hardest places in our culture and said what too many others were afraid to say, even when the crowd was hostile and the odds were against him. He understood that if America is going to be renewed, the next generation has to find its way back to faith, truth, and love of country. That's one reason JD Vance's story meant so much to him: Charlie saw in the Vice President something rare in public life -- a man whose faith had been tested, shaken, and ultimately rebuilt. That journey is what JD Vance writes about in his new book,Communion: Finding My Way Back to Faith. Peter, this book isn't just about JD Vance's story... It speaks to something much bigger happening in our country right now. So many Americans know what it feels like to live in a culture that is constantly pulling them away from what matters most -- away from faith, from family, and from the values that once held this country together. Young people face that pressure every single day. They're told faith is outdated. They're told truth is whatever feels right, or whatever the culture says it is. JD Vance knows what it is like to live in that confusion. He knows what it is like to search, to be shaped by a broken culture, and by God's grace, to find his way back. That's what Communion is about... And it gets to the heart of what so many families are watching happen in the lives of their children and grandchildren right now. That's why Turning Point USA is reaching young people where this battle is actually being fought -- on campuses, in classrooms, and in a culture that keeps pressuring them to walk away from faith. Your support does far more than just send you a book... It helps Turning Point USA reach young people in the very places where faith is under attack. Because of supporters like you, students on more than 5,000 campuses are hearing something they may not hear anywhere else: a serious defense of faith, truth, and a life rooted in God. For many of them, that's the first time anyone has challenged the lies they have been fed. And for many of them, that's where their minds begin to change -- and so do their lives. Charlie believed the next generation was worth fighting for. He believed young people were not beyond reach -- they needed someone willing to meet them where this battle is being fought and tell them the truth clearly and directly. That's why your support matters. It helps Turning Point USA keep showing up. And it helps carry forward the mission Charlie gave his life to build. | | | Now's the time to act. Now's the time to restore faith in God and faith in America before another generation drifts even farther from both. And with you, Charlie's mission will reach further -- and touch more young lives -- than ever before. For Charlie, The Turning Point USA Team P.S. Peter, many young people leave home with a foundation of faith, only to have the culture chip away at it, piece by piece. JD Vance knows what that struggle looks like. | [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/117915?t=6&akid=26395%2E878179%2Egapz0o) Friend, I’m humbled that Iowans have put their faith in me to serve as their Democratic nominee for the U.S. Senate. And I’m humbled by all the amazing supporters who invested in our campaign to make it happen.

But winning the primary forced us to take risks and use all our resources. That means to win this race we’re relying on grassroots donors like you to help us refill our campaign coffers.

**The Senate majority is on the line, so this is urgent: Can I count on you to rush a $7 contribution split between my campaign and Voter Protection Project to ensure we have the resources to flip Iowa blue?** | [RUSH A DONATION! »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/117915?t=7&akid=26395%2E878179%2Egapz0o)

I’ll level with you, team: **Even though Democrats' path to the Senate majority rolls through Iowa, we’re still underdogs in this must-win race.**

A big part of that is money. My Republican opponent Ashley Hinson has taken millions from corporate PACs, so she entered the General Election with over $6 million in the bank.

_And that’s before the shady dark money Republican Super PACs spend their $40 million warchest._

But the thing is, I’m no stranger to tough fights.

I wasn’t supposed to win my Iowa State House races. I went door to door, crawling up stairs, dragging my wheelchair after me to talk to voters face-to-face.

_That’s how I won a deep-red Trump district._**_Twice._**

If I had time in this campaign to drag myself up to every front porch in Iowa, believe me, I would. But I don’t. The only way we can win is to keep getting our message out on airwaves across Iowa.

And to do that, we need money. Today. Not in a month or even two weeks. Right now.

[So will you help split a donation today to make sure we have the immediate resources to get back on the air and ensure Ashley Hinson and the Republican Super PACs can’t drown out our positive message of change?](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/117915?t=8&akid=26395%2E878179%2Egapz0o)

Peter,

I’ve shown what determined leadership can accomplish.

In California, I’ve passed hundreds of laws that helped build thousands of affordable homes, capped insulin copays at $35, expanded mental health care, protected LGBTQ people and immigrants, strengthened public transit, and stopped ICE agents from hiding behind masks.

**Now, I’m running for Congress to take those wins to Donald Trump’s doorstep. More than that - It’s time to turn proven California solutions into national progress.**

We have a big agenda and I’ve heard from a lot of you that housing is the first thing I need to tackle. Others have said in the wake of the resurgence of ICE violence that we must stop Donald Trump and turn our attention to immigration reform.

**Reality is - we have to do all of it - all at once.

I still need to know: what is most important to you right now. If the next Congress accomplishes one thing - what must it be?**

Hi, Peter – It continues to be an honor to run for governor, and as I travel around our beautiful state, I'm loving all of these opportunities to meet and connect with so many Vermonters. I don't think anyone will be surprised to learn that one of the issues I hear the most about is health care. So I'm reaching out today to tell you more about [**my plan**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135341528/633921917/-750528621?refcode=ea.52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ms=ea.52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTJjODYxMDgtOWU4MC1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=R1kPoqVoo7dO8PQISWILXUead08iLc5Xtwx06gcGtdA=&emci=ab7ad704-8080-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1745378) to treat our health care crisis like the emergency it is. ([**Click here**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135341529/633921918/-803653937?v=jGITb4cWU9o&refcode=ea.52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ms=ea.52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTJjODYxMDgtOWU4MC1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=R1kPoqVoo7dO8PQISWILXUead08iLc5Xtwx06gcGtdA=&emci=ab7ad704-8080-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1745378) to watch my mini-podcast, Tell Me More with Aly Richards. Episode two is all about health care!) Let's start with a fundamental truth: **Health care is a human right.** No one should have to choose between having food on the table and seeking the health care they need. And yet, our health care system is failing Vermonters. We have the highest individual premiums in the country, and too many Vermonters aren’t able to access critical care in their communities. We have to act now to transform our health care system; Vermonters can’t afford to wait. | [**READ MY PLAN**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135341530/633921919/-750528621?refcode=ea.52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ms=ea.52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTJjODYxMDgtOWU4MC1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=R1kPoqVoo7dO8PQISWILXUead08iLc5Xtwx06gcGtdA=&emci=ab7ad704-8080-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1745378)
---
Here’s how we do it, together:
First, we must **ensure universal access to primary care.** Every Vermonter deserves a primary care provider; not as a privilege, but as a guarantee. I have a real plan to ensure access to primary care and control costs without losing access to critical services.
* Grow our workforce of primary care providers, including doctors and skilled nurses, by offering rural incentive pay, providing student loan forgiveness, building a homegrown workforce pipeline by partnering with our local education partners, and getting primary care providers out of the business of handling insurance.
* Expand our free clinic model. There are currently eight free clinics in Vermont providing free, high-quality care to their communities. I will work with service providers, municipalities, patient advocates, and others to map out the ideal locations for additional clinics so that everyone who needs one can reasonably access these vital services.

**I will also fight for every federal health care dollar Vermont is owed.** The federal government owes Vermont billions in health care funding, and I won’t leave a single dollar on the table. I’ll fight back against any attempt to cut the benefits Vermonters have earned, and make sure every dollar of our Rural Health Transformation funding works for Vermont families.
**Finally, I will build a multi-year plan with our hospitals to keep costs low and quality high** by bringing folks together to create a path to sustainability for hospitals and reliable services for patients. We need to organize to thrive instead of scrambling to survive.
We _can_ get our health care system back on track. I've said it before, and I'll say it again: [**the solutions**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/135341531/633921920/-750528621?refcode=ea.52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ms=ea.52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjMvMS8xMjQ5NTciLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNTJjODYxMDgtOWU4MC1mMTExLWIzMzctMDAwZDNhMTU1OGNlIiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=R1kPoqVoo7dO8PQISWILXUead08iLc5Xtwx06gcGtdA=&emci=ab7ad704-8080-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&emdi=52c86108-9e80-f111-b337-000d3a1558ce&ceid=1745378) to our most significant challenges are within reach. It just takes focus, collaboration, and moving together toward a defined result. That's how I led the push for affordable child care in Vermont, and that's how I'll lead on health care transformation.
